item.title: Victor Wembanyama makes history by being the first player in 50 years with these numbers
item.description: Victor Wembanyama makes history by being the first player in 50 years with these numbers originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . In a 14-game slate on Wednesday, there were plenty of top-tier performances. Luka Doncic was once again brilliant for the Los Angeles Lakers with a 40-point night, and the same could be said about Denver Nuggets star Nikola Jokic with another triple-double to his name. Despite those amazing performances, they all pale in comparison when compared to San Antonio Spurs superstar Victor Wembanyama. The Frenchman had the night's best performance, posting a stat line of 52 points, 24 rebounds, and eight blocks to beat the Dallas Mavericks in a close game. Victor Wembanyama puts up historic numbers against the Mavericks For almost the entire game, the Spurs were in control against the Mavericks on Wednesday. That was why people were raving about Wembanyama in the first half, as he already had 29 points, 15 rebounds, and five blocks at halftime. However, the Mavericks staged a comeback in the second half. They almost won the game with a Kyrie Irving game-winner, but the Spurs defended it well, which led to a victory that complemented Wembanyama's performance. MORE: Victor Wembanyama goes viral for three blocks in 13 seconds It was a magical night for the French giant, and it seems that his teammates agree with that. Everyone knows he is the Spurs' superstar, so if he performs well, the atmosphere within the Spurs organization is much better. "When he gets in the vicinity of the paint, he’s just unstoppable to guard. So I mean we just gotta keep on finding ways to get him down there and then let him operate," Spurs guard Dylan Harper said about Wembanyama's impressive performance . Wembanyama is playing at an MVP level once again, as the Spurs have won their sixth straight game. After their slow start to the season, the Spurs fans were worried, but now, it seems that the Spurs have everyone else worried. item.title: WWE Crown Jewel 2026 match predictions, expert picks for every matchup in Riyadh
item.description: WWE Crown Jewel 2026 match predictions, expert picks for every matchup in Riyadh originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . WWE returns to Saudi Arabia for the latest Crown Jewel event. The event will feature title bouts, with WWE's marquee players competing for bragging rights. Two WWE Crown Jewel Championship belts are on the line. Champions from Raw and SmackDown face off for more gold. Roman Reigns, Sami Zayn, Liv Morgan, and Chelsea Green all have something to prove. Meanwhile, a rivalry looks to be settled when Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton compete in a Last Man Standing match. The tag team titles are also on the line. Here's a breakdown of all the action and predictions for who will win at the latest Crown Jewel event. WWE Crown Jewel 2026 match predictions Roman Reigns (Raw Champion) vs. Sami Zayn (SmackDown Champion) for the WWE Crown Jewel Championship Reigns and Zayn renew their story from a few years ago. This time, Zayn is a champion. Reigns has put on great performances in 2026, but he’s been preoccupied with the 946 group. Zayn has enemies left and right as champion, but Reigns and The Bloodline have had a tough time with Royce Keys, Bronco Nima, Lucien Prince, Carmelo Hayes, Jaida Parker, and now Cruz Montana. There’s no doubt Reigns and Zayn will have a good match that starts slow and ends with a bang. However, expect interference at the highest level, from 946 and The Bloodline. Zayn will take advantage of all the chaos and sneak in a win. Sporting News prediction: Sami Zayn Liv Morgan (Raw Champion) vs. Chelsea Green (SmackDown Champion) for the WWE Crown Jewel Championship Chelsea Green has proven to be a fighting champion since getting the interim tag off her reign. She has had to keep an eye on friend and Money in the Bank winner Tiffany Stratton. Liv Morgan, a previous Crown Jewel Champion, has been untouchable with The Judgment Day in her corner. The story of Stratton holding the briefcase is almost too similar to her 2024 run with it. Given that, WWE could potentially give fans a shocking twist. Stratton could cash in on Green after Morgan beats her, potentially thanks to Stratton stabbing her friend in the back. Sporting News prediction: Liv Morgan Cody Rhodes vs. Randy Orton in a Last Man Standing match Rhodes retained the Undisputed WWE Championship against Orton at WrestleMania 42 in a match that featured Pat McAfee. While it wasn’t well received, the end, Orton punting Rhodes unconscious, was. Now, months later, the two are feuding again. This time, Rhodes must punt Orton in the head. Rhodes almost did it at Sunday Night's Main Event but hesitated. He did it to Baron Corbin. The story of Orton getting his comeuppance has been building for a while. Rhodes will hesitate before executing, leading to one big crescendo of a finish. It’s the only way the match should end. item.title: Match Preview: Sunderland v Dinamo Zagreb — More European Fireworks On Wearside
item.description: SUNDERLAND, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 04: Regis Le Bris, Manager of Sunderland, reacts as he interacts with Chemsdine Talbi during the training session on MD-1 ahead of the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD4, at The Academy of Light on November 04, 2026 in Sunderland, England. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) | Getty Images Thursday 5th November 2026 Sunderland v Dinamo Zagreb – Europa League Poznań Stadium – Kick-Off: 20:00 Match Coverage TV/Stream: Full live match coverage is available via TNT Sports. Radio: Full live match commentary available via BBC Radio Newcastle (not online) It feels like a long time since we took on AZ Alkmaar to bring European football back to Wearside, but this’s our second night of fireworks at the Stadium of Light, and it falls on Bonfire Night. A lot has happened since then. One thing that hasn’t happened, however, is a Premier League victory. Just one point from a possible 15 has been taken since we kicked off our continental adventure on home soil. Unfortunately, it has the potential to take the shine off our performance so far in the Europa League, and until we improve, any European game will be placed into the context of the two league games either side of it. But here we are, 9th in the table and on the same points as Juventus; we’re still unbeaten, and we’ve got a great chance of progressing to the knockouts. The news this week has been mixed since our capitulation at Coventry at the weekend. Let’s go with the bad news first, and Habib Diarra has been ruled out for around six weeks. You feel for the lad to start with because he just can’t catch a break, and then there’s the aspect that he was a player who potentially gave us an option to freshen things up either tonight or at the weekend. But, for all of those chanting his name recently, Chemsdine Talbi has replaced him in the European squad. Again, all eyes will be on the starting line-up, not just for tonight, but for clues of what we’ll do at the weekend. Our opponents tonight are Croatian champions Dinamo Zagreb, and they sacked their manager this week, which might mean a lot of our scouting reports go in the bin. They’ve beaten Anderlecht, drew against Hapoel Be’er Sheva and lost against NAC Nijmegen. On the domestic front, they have won the league 19 times in the last 21 seasons. Which is pretty impressive. Last season, they reached the knockout phase, but were beaten at the first hurdle by Genk during extra time in the second leg. The year before last, they narrowly missed out on the knockout phase of the Champions League by goal difference, where they beat AC Milan and Salzburg on the way. We shouldn’t expect it to go all our way tonight. The betting… The bookies have the Lads at 4/9 to win the game, while Zagreb are 5/1 for the victory, and the draw is 17/5. Prediction… Sunderland 2-1 Dinamo Zagreb The bookies might fancy us for a routine victory tonight, but I think it’s going to be a tough test. I think we’ll come out on top, and if we do come

item.title: Seven Changes for Sunderland For Tonight’s Game Against Zagreb?
item.description: SUNDERLAND, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 04: Regis Le Bris, Manager of Sunderland, speaks with his staff including First Team Coach Jose Fonte during the training session on MD-1 ahead of the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD4, at The Academy of Light on November 04, 2026 in Sunderland, England. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) | Getty Images What lessons have been learned from Saturday? What have the honest and frank conversations produced? We’ll find out in a matter of hours as the lads are back in action against Zagreb. Hopefully, we’ll see a huge change in attitude and application, as well as our intent and team cohesion, which has been sorely lacking in recent weeks. Le Bris has been given a stay of execution – will he take advantage of it? We’ll soon find out. Goalkeeper: Robin Roefs Roefs can’t be happy at present playing in front of a team that’s continually leaving him exposed – he’s produced some great saves in recent European games and hopefully he has a good night tonight. Defence: Thomas Meunier, Kevin Danso, Luke O’Nien, Dayann Methalie Trai Hume has played a lot of football recently and with an international break looming that’ll continue. Meunier needs a game so should hopefully start at right back, while Methalie will start on the left. A good show from him tonight could see him line up against Chelsea. In the centre, we’re likely to see Danso return – Mukiele is still out – while O’Nien could play alongside him. The other option is Alderete, but he’s completely out of sorts and needs to be taken out for a while. Midfield: Nilson Angulo, Granit Xhaka, Jules Ahoka, Chemsdine Talbi, Malick Fofana Talbi’s inclusion in the squad is a boost and he will surely come into the team – I’d like to see him play in the 10 as he looked good there against Brentford. I think this is a game Xhaka ideally would sit out, but his form and the troubles the team’s having means he probably should play; hopefully alongside Ahoka, who can provide legs and energy around him. On the wings, we need to go with two proper wingers, so hopefully Fofana will produce a good display on the left, and Angulo can carry on his good work against Poznan on the right. Striker: Wilson Isidor We don’t need to risk Brobbey, so Isidor should get an hour after 30 minutes at Coventry – he’s more than capable of causing teams problems, as long as the set up behind his is decent.

item.title: New CBA proposal adjusts salary cap, floor
item.description: ATLANTA, GA - MAY 13: A locked padlock and chain against two official MLB baseballs representing a potential lockout between Major League Baseball (MLB) and the Major League Baseball Players Association (MLBPA) for the 2027 MLB season, as photographed on May 13, 2026 in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by David J. Griffin/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Major League Baseball has amended its salary cap and floor proposal to the MLB Players Association. Now that the 2026 season is complete and baseball is into its offseason, MLB has proposed delaying the start of the salary cap and floor to the 2028 season. The rest of their proposals would begin with the 2027 season but the teams would have a full season to make adjustments to prepare themselves for the coming changes. The owners further proposed increasing the cap to $258.2 million from the original $245.3 million and the floor to $180.2 million from $171.2 million. The new numbers reflect a 50-50 split of the projected revenue for the 2028 season. A change to the retirement proposal The offer also includes $282 million in luxury tax revenue to be given to players in cash payments instead of being placed into retirement benefits. In the present system, when a team pays luxury tax, half of the money goes into player benefits and the other half to the teams. For the 2027 season, the league is offering to pay the retirement portion directly to the players. According to league estimates , $285,000 would go to each player who received a full year of service time, $213,400 to a player with three-quarters of a year of service, $142,300 to a player with a half year of service, and $71,100 to any player with a quarter year of service. Teams outside the guidelines Per the MLB numbers, 12 teams would have to raise payroll to meet the minimum proposed floor while eight teams would have to decrease their payroll to meet the cap. Those numbers are based on current payrolls and would change based on what teams spend in 2027. Players response The MLB Players Association predictably responded negatively to the new offer. “MLB owners continue to propose blowing up the current system and replacing it with one designed to line their pockets and increase their franchise values.” The statement continued, “a massive reduction in player compensation, elimination of fundamental player rights, plus a gutting of domestic and international amateur entry systems.” A statement virtually identical to the previous proposal from the owners. Sweetening the pot? This appears to be an attempt by the league to sweeten the deal for the players but doesn’t seem to have the desired effect. The baseline for the union is their unwillingness to accept a salary cap and floor as the start of negotiations. The current contract expires and 11:59 pm eastern time on Dec. 1. The owners have made it clear they intend to lock the players out if no deal is reached by that time.

item.title: What Can Sunderland Expect From Croatian Champions Dinamo Zagreb?
item.description: ZAGREB, CROATIA - OCTOBER 22: Iker Almena of GNK Dinamo Zagreb and Luka Ivanusec of GNK Dinamo Zagreb during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between GNK Dinamo and N.E.C. Nijmegen at Stadion Maksimir on October 22, 2026 in Zagreb, Croatia. (Photo by Josip Regovic/Pixsell/MB Media/Getty Images) | Getty Images Dinamo won both the Croatian league and cup last season under Mario Kovačević. How would you reflect on that campaign and what were the expectations among supporters heading into this season? Last season’s campaign went about as well as Dinamo wanted after not winning anything the season prior; they dominated and returned to their usual form. They always want to win the domestic double; they essentially take it for granted. So the real challenges/expectations come in Europe, with them being back in the UCL qualifiers; the club and the fans want to return to the UCL. This didn’t happen, as they lost to the Norwegian side, Viking, because of their poor defensive lapses in concentration, as they conceded two goals in quick succession in both legs. This left the fans mad at the higher-ups for not bringing in immediate improvements for the squad beforehand, and at the coach for the poor reactions from the team. Dinamo currently sit second behind Hajduk in the league and Saturday’s shock 1-0 defeat to Rudeš ultimately proved to be Mario Kovačević’s final match. What has gone wrong in recent weeks? It’s just the players’ form; everybody except Dion Drena Beljo is struggling to play at a good level game after game. The defence, especially, has been the most inconsistent. Consistently losing their man or having poor reactions inside the box. Kovačević has tried to tweak a few things, with some changes to the starting XIs here and there, but nothing has clicked. Even if a player performed well in one match, the next, he doesn’t. Kovačević left the club by mutual consent just four days before the trip to Sunderland despite winning the double last season. Were you surprised by that decision and do you think it was the right one? Not surprised by the decision at all; it was a long time coming, as in September fans were already calling for his departure after really poor performances vs. Istra, Osijek and Hapoel Be’er Sheva. Even in victories, Dinamo were unconvincing and barely got them over the line, as they were put under serious pressure by Gorica and Lokomotiv, for example. I think it’s the right decision, because at the end of the day, Kovačević has struggled a LOT and hasn’t delivered after saying time and time again, “We need to improve next match,” and that never happened. It seems like the pressure of a bad slump really got to him, since it’s the first one he’s had that is this bad. But the board of Dinamo also has to answer for a shocking transfer window where they made no real signings ahead of the UCL play-off, signing all their real squad assets after they had been knocked out. item.title: OTD (5/11/1938): Gallacher Scores Final Goals As Sunderland Claim Season’s First Home Win
item.description: Patsy Gallacher, Sunderland (Photo by Barratts/PA Images via Getty Images) | PA Images via Getty Images While 1937 is rightly remembered for Sunderland’s first FA Cup win, in league terms the season hadn’t been a success – at least compared to the previous campaign. After claiming the title in 1936, the lads finished the 36/37 season in eighth place – 13 points behind winners Manchester City – and finished in the same position the following season, albeit just eight points shy of champions Arsenal. The FA Cup had once again been in tantalising grasp – only for Huddersfield Town to snatch the potential of the holders retaining the trophy with a semi-final defeat. 1938/39 began with a renewed determination to reclaim the title – or at least seriously compete for it – but on this day in 1938, Sunderland finally won their first home game of the season on their sixth attempt – climbing to 6th position in the top flight in the process. Unbeknown to anyone watching on that day, it would be the highest we’d rank in the table for eight years – and it signalled the end of an era for this talented Sunderland team. The 38/39 season saw us finish 16th, only six points off a relegation spot, after a run of just 5 wins in the season’s remaining 22 games saw us drift down the table, and the following season was curtailed due to the outbreak of WW2. But on this day back in 1938, things seemed a lot brighter as the final whistle went. A Sunderland team featuring eight of the 11 who’d played at Wembley 18 months earlier had comprehensively beaten Stoke City 3-0, turning in an excellent performance that saw Patsy Gallacher net his 100th goal in league football. He’d been on 99 since scoring away at Grimsby in March – and typically went on to score his 101st just eight minutes later. Or did he? We’ll get back to that momentarily. By the time Gallacher got his first of the game in the 40th minute. the Sunderland team – missing only Bert Johnston, Sandy McNab and Len Duns from the 1937 side – were one up. Sunderland had started the game excellently. Bobby Gurney and Eddie Burbanks were denied by keeper Norman Wilkinson before, on five minutes, Johnny Spuhler had a goal chalked off for offside. Raich Carter then hit the underside of the crossbar with a great strike, which Sunderland claimed had crossed the line, but to no avail. The ball was most definitely over the line on 15, however. Carter ran onto a through ball from Hastings, showed great strength to hold off a defender and lashed the ball into the roof of the net from the edge of the box. The lead was almost immediately doubled; Gallacher drove the ball just wide after being set up by Burbanks. Stoke were posing a threat – England winger Stanley Matthews put in a teasing centre that Mapson dealt well with. Sunderland had a scare when Alex Hastings appeared to be knocked unconscious heading the ball away. item.title: An Introduction to Dinamo Zagreb: What Can Sunderland Expect?
item.description: On the occasion of the International tie Day at Saint Mark's square in front of Saint Mark church on upper town, Honour Cravat Regiment changing the guard on 18 Oct 2014, Zagreb,Croatia. (Photo by Alen Gurovic/NurPhoto) (Photo by NurPhoto/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Tonight, Sunderland play their second Europa League home game of the campaign, as the Lads welcome Dinamo Zagreb to Wearside. Here’s what you need to know about the Croatian champions! Zagreb: Croatia’s Capital With a population of around 750,000, Zagreb is Croatia’s largest city, and the use of its name dates back nearly 1000 years to 1094 AD. The city emerged from two medieval settlements (Gric and Kaptol) and began rapid development and expansion when the two combined in the 19th century. It has played a crucial role in the political history of Croatia, and in 1941 it became the capital of a Croatian puppet state controlled by the Axis powers. After being freed in 1945, Croatia became a part of Yugoslavia from the end of the Second World War until 1991. Zagreb was the centre of a newly independent Croatia during and following the Croatian War of Independence (1991-1995). On a lighter note, Zagreb is home to the world’s shortest public transport funicular, which connects the city’s old town to its newer Novi Zagreb area. It spans a total of 66m, and between its opening in 1890 to 1934, it was powered by steam. Nowadays, the journey is electrified and lasts approximately a minute. The city also keeps many of its old traditions. Every day at noon, a cannon is fired from Lotrščak Tower beside the funicular to mark midday. This has happened every day since 1877. Zagreb also has over 200 gas street lamps which are still lit manually every night, and this tradition dates back to 1863. There are also a number of weird and wonderful museums to visit in the Croatian capital. These include the Museum of Hangovers, the Museum of Laughter, the Museum of Broken Relationships, and a mushroom museum. Dinamo Zagreb: A Brief History Dinamo Zagreb were initially formed in 1911 when Croatia was a part of the Austro-Hungarian Empire. Upon the end of the Second World War, the club was dissolved by communist authorities; however, it was re-established just three days later on the ninth of June, 1945. The new club inherited the colours, nickname, badge and fanbase of the original club. Its name was changed to Croatia Zagreb in 1993 – a move which was seen as a political move to move away from the club’s communist past amidst Croatian independence. However, this name was never accepted by supporters, and the name Dinamo Zagreb was reinstated in the year 2000. Dinamo Zagreb is Croatia’s most successful club and has lifted the Croatian league 25 times, most recently last season, in which they finished 20 points ahead of second-placed Hajduk Split. They have also won the Croatian Cup and Super Cup a record 18 and eight times respectively, as well as nine Yugoslav League titles and e

item.title: The Régis Rebirth — Can Le Bris Find The Magic Formula For Sunderland?
item.description: SUNDERLAND, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 28: Regis Le Bris, head coach of Sunderland reacts on the sidelines during the Carabao Cup Fourth Round match between Sunderland and Brentford at Stadium of Light on October 28, 2026 in Sunderland, England. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’ve all seen how things have gone wrong over the last few days, weeks and months and a lot of errors could be attributed to Régis Le Bris over that period. It looks like the club are backing Le Bris for at least a little bit longer in the hope that he can figure the whole mess out and get some points on the board. Whether you agree with the decision or not, I’m sure many of you have some opinions on how he should go about changing our fortunes, and I’m no different! So, I thought it would be fun to have a look at some things he may consider to flip the script for the Lads in the coming weeks with the fair caveat that although I think these are fair points to raise, I believe that Le Bris is a truly gifted manager with more knowledge and experience of the game than I could ever hope to possess. For that reason, I’ll be offering some counters to each point for a bit of balance. Pick a style First up for me is to pick a style and to stick to it. To my eyes, it looks like we have no clear sense of direction or intention in our play anymore. When we have the ball, we often pass it from side to side without incision. When we don’t, we sit deeply without any quick players to counter incisively. We’ve seemingly lost our patterns of play, our triangles and a clear way of moving through the thirds dangerously, and it looks like Le Bris is stuck between two styles at the moment. Disregarding his first five or so games in charge wherein he employed a wonderfully intense press in the Championship, he’s has generally and successfully set us up as a defensively solid team that’s clinical in transition. We recruited for this, as well — big defenders without much passing range, record signing Habib Diarra, whose primary attribute is carrying the ball at pace, and quick wingers that could hurt teams on the break. We soak up pressure and we punish teams for committing too much, or at least we used to. To me, it looks like Le Bris has tried to evolve this style and introduce some more possession-based, expansive traits into our play over the last few months. You could see it starting ever since we breached our forty point target last season, and with a couple of slip-ups here and there, it was a smooth transition with impressive results. Fast forward to the present day, though, and it’s a mess, with a a slow and tedious attack, a dreadful defensive record and a non-existent midfield. We’re getting the worst of all worlds at the moment and I think that if Le Bris wants to succeed, he must bring it back to basics and introduce some pace for the counter or change tact altogether and find a different way for Sunderland to impose themselves on our opponents in the interests of chance cr

item.title: ‘You can’t win a Super Bowl…’: Calvin Johnson revisits Lions’ biggest mistake
item.description: Photo by Raj Mehta/Getty Images Calvin Johnson believes the Detroit Lions have had the talent to win a Super Bowl but insists they cannot reach the NFL’s biggest prize without being willing to spend big. The former wide receiver pointed to Matthew Stafford’s departure as an example of why Detroit needed to be more aggressive in building a championship-winning roster. Johnson spent his entire NFL career with the Lions before retiring at just 30 years old, but his relationship with the organisation has improved considerably in recent years. Calvin Johnson says Detroit Lions cannot win Super Bowl on a budget Speaking on the Chasing No. 1 podcast, Johnson explained why he believed Detroit had the necessary pieces during his time with the franchise. “The biggest thing for me is that, I used to always say, we tell everybody we got the team here in Detroit. We had the dudes, but you can’t win a Super Bowl on a budget, man. You got to go all in.” Johnson also pointed to teams making significant moves to add the final pieces needed to compete for a championship. He then brought up Stafford, who won the Super Bowl with the Los Angeles Rams in his first season after leaving Detroit. “We had most of the pieces there in Detroit. And so for me, when he won Super Bowl, literally the first year after he left Detroit, I’m out there like, ‘I mean, I told y’all what we had.’” Stafford’s success with the Rams reinforced Johnson’s belief that the Lions had been closer to competing for a title than their lack of championship success suggested. With the NFL trade deadline approaching, Detroit fans are hoping general manager Brad Holmes can strengthen the roster as the team looks to maintain its position in the NFC North. Johnson’s comments also come after years of tension between him and the Lions following his retirement. The organisation once sought $1.6 million back from his signing bonus after he walked away before completing his contract. However, those differences have since faded. Johnson has returned to Ford Field to support the team and has earned places on the Lions’ All-Time Team and Ring of Honor. Now, with Detroit still chasing its first Super Bowl title, his message remains clear: having the talent is not enough if the organisation is unwilling to make the moves needed to finish the job. item.title: Texas women beat Fairleigh Dickinson to open season, but clearly are a work in progress
item.description: Madison Booker, Texas' go-to player after a wave of offseason personnel losses, led the way with 24 points in Wednesday's season-opening win over Fairleigh Dickinson in Austin. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) AUSTIN - Rori Harmon doesn't live here any more. Neither, in fact, do Jordan Lee or Aaliyah Crump or Justice Carlton . Kyla Oldacre? She gone. Instead, Vic Schaefer introduced six new players to the crowd of 9,688 fans at Moody Center before a strange season opener that resembled very little of last season's team that fell to eventual national champion UCLA in the Final Four semifinals last April. It would have been seven but freshman forward Brihanna Crittendon suffered an eye injury in Wednesday's shootaround and unavailable for the first game of the year. The growing pains were obvious. And Schaefer made no bones about the need to improve almost overnight after watching his No. 6 Longhorns struggle - relatively speaking by the coach's standards - in an uneven 85-65 win over a solid Fairleigh Dickinson. "We didn't play very well defensively," Schaefer said. "They got off 20 3s on us, and we pride ourselves on pressure and denying shots, and most of them were wide open. They weren't even contested." Sign up for Kirk Bohls' newsletter Sign up for Kirk Bohls' new newsletter for news, exclusive analysis and insights on University of Texas sports. Texas' seventh-year head coach didn't rip his young team, which includes five freshmen, three of whom were McDonald's All-Americans. He never raised his voice and didn't look frustrated. He's well aware last year's 35-4 club that reached back-to-back Final Fours offered his best chance to win his first national championship. Harmon's playing in Turkey these days after being waived by the Washington Mystics after appearing in just 10 games but still part of its developmental squad. Lee's playing for Schaefer nemesis, Dawn Staley, at South Carolina. The sharp-shooting Crump is making jumpers for Duke. Carlton was supposed to be the headliner for the Houston Cougars but blew out a knee and is done for the year . Oldacre is a free agent but got some time in WNBA camps. Still, the Longhorns were picked to finish second behind the Gamecocks in the SEC media preseason poll, which in itself is a remarkable tribute to Texas after five of the team's seven best players have departed. Texas Longhorns forward Madison Booker (35) and guard Zya Vann (9) battle Fairleigh Dickinson Knights guard Ane Valle (11) for the rebound in the second half of the Texas Longhorns' 85-65 win over the Fairleigh Dickinson Knights at the Moody Center in Austin, Nov. 4, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) It was very obvious this is a new team with new talents and different personalities. item.title: South Carolina QB LaNorris Sellers is spending fall semester working at a golf course?
item.description: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images South Carolina QB LaNorris Sellers is spending fall semester working at a golf course? appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . South Carolina football quarterback LaNorris Sellers needs a quiet place when he’s not leading the Gamecocks. Even amid boosting his NFL Draft stock after shredding Oklahoma on Saturday . But his peaceful venue happens to be his side hustle: Working at a local golf center, which he shared to ESPN. South Carolina QB LaNorris Sellers isn't attending classes this semester, but instead working at a golf center ⛳ Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) He shares more about the job with @itsthebaldgirl ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/Bux9wta2pQ — SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) November 4, 2026 Sellers is employed at Par Tee Golf Center in nearby West Columbia. The links also keeps him away from the classroom on the South Carolina campus. Because Sellers doesn’t have a regular class schedule like the rest of his teammates. Instead, Sellers is using the golf center for his required internship before officially graduating. It’s all part of his sports and entertainment management degree he’s pursuing. So what duties does Sellers perform when he’s not dissecting defenses and going after them with his arm and legs? He’s performing the traditional labor involved with golf course workers: Picking up golf balls from the range, plus cutting grass. Now Sellers is almost complete with his internship at the driving range. Perhaps a spot at The Masters in Augusta, Georgia could be in his future, especially if that renown event needs additional help. But outside of seeing golf swings, Sellers and South Carolina is taking a big swing at staying alive in the College Football Playoff race. The Gamecocks managed to sneak into the top 25 of the CFP poll released on Tuesday. South Carolina’s upset over a previously No. 11 ranked Tennessee team certainly helps the Gamecocks’ case. Sellers and SC are one of three teams with three losses to make it inside the postseason rankings, joining Florida and Oregon. item.title: Wemby magic powers Spurs past Mavs as Sixers roll on
item.description: Victor Wembanyama scored a career-high 52 points as San Antonio defeated the Dallas Mavericks (Ronald Cortes) Victor Wembanyama produced a career-high 52-point performance as the San Antonio Spurs battled past the Dallas Mavericks 112-111 on Wednesday. French superstar Wembanyama, whose previous best was a 50-point display in 2024, dominated at both ends of the court to power San Antonio to their sixth win of the season. Wembanyama's masterpiece included a record-breaking first-half that saw him reach the interval with 29 points, 15 rebounds, five blocks and two steals. The 22-year-old would go on to finish with 52 points, 24 rebounds and eight blocks as San Antonio held off a ferocious second-half rally to claim victory. Wembanyama, who was backed by 21 points from Dylan Harper and 17 from Stephon Castle, praised San Antonio's "relentless" approach. "We did mostly the right thing, the most ambitious," Wembanyama told ESPN. "It was just relentless. We wanted it more tonight." Asked about his own performance, Wembanyama replied: "It's very good because I'm trying to show the example." Team-mate Harper paid tribute to Wembanyama's professionalism. "Just the mentality, the dedication, the discipline he has every day that he comes into the gym with is unmatched," Harper told ESPN. Kyrie Irving led the Mavericks scoring with 29 points, including five three-pointers. - Sixers down Pistons - Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid combined for 56 points as the Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Detroit Pistons 112-106 in their top-of-the-table Eastern Conference clash. Brown finished with 30 points and Embiid added 26 to give the Sixers another impressive road win that moved them to 8-1 at the top of the standings, with Detroit (6-2) in second. Brown and Embiid led another balanced offensive performance from Philadelphia, who saw all five starters reach double figures. LeBron James added a double-double with 13 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists while Tyrese Maxey drained three three-pointers on his way to a 19-point haul. Brown, who arrived from the Boston Celtics in the offseason, said he was "still adjusting" to his new team-mates. "I'm still figuring it out," Brown said, before paying tribute to the performance of 41-year-old team-mate James. "LeBron has been great," Brown said. "To see what he's doing at his age makes sense for LeBron James, but for nobody else would it make sense." The Sixers moved into the lead towards the end of the first quarter and kept their noses in front for the remainder of the game, stretching the lead to 18 points before a late rally from Detroit. Duncan Robinson led the Pistons with 27 points while Cade Cunningham added 26. The reigning champion New York Knicks scored their biggest win of the season with a 135-105 blowout over the Chicago Bulls at Madison Square Garden. item.title: Como boss Cesc Fabregas admits he was 'angry' to concede despite breaking Italian away scoring record in 9-1 Champions League win at Lens
item.description: FBL-EUR-C1-LENS-COMO - AFP Como head coach Cesc Fabregas expressed frustration over failing to keep a clean sheet even after watching his side dismantle Lens 9-1 on Wednesday night. No Italian club had previously managed seven away goals in European Cup or Champions League history before the Serie A visitors ran riot in France. Italian visitors rewrite history books Fabregas saw his maiden Champions League away win slightly soured by a second-half consolation strike as Como recorded their sixth consecutive victory across all competitions. Having beaten RB Leipzig and Manchester United 4-1 at home either side of a 3-2 loss at Feyenoord, the visitors climbed to fourth in the standings despite missing Moise Kean, Trevoh Chalobah, Assane Diao, Jesus Rodriguez and Jayden Addai. Tournament top scorer Tasos Douvikas netted a treble to score in all four European outings, while Nico Paz, Lucas Da Cunha, Marc-Oliver Kempf, Mattia Liberali, Martin Baturina and 18-year-old debutant Matteo Papaccioli also struck. Manager urges humility after rout Speaking to Sky Sport Italia about sitting fourth midway through the league phase, Fabregas smiled: "It is also our fourth ever Champions League game, so four is the key number here. "I'm happy, this is football and everything went our way. The lads did well, now we have to prepare for a very important match on Sunday, the ninth in a run between breaks for international duty." Urging his young squad to stay grounded after their historic display, the Spaniard added: "It is a wonderful night for Como, for all our fans and many lads here who are at the start of their careers, but they need to keep their feet on the ground, be humble, keep learning and not think everything will go well from here on. "They must keep working to continue these performances." Defensive lapse frustrates former midfielder Despite almost every goal coming from slick passing moves out from the back and an early penalty against Maxence Caqueret being overturned by VAR, Como are still waiting for their first European shutout after conceding a 65th-minute corner volley. Reflecting on that solitary blemish, Fabregas confessed: "I am angry over the goal we conceded, as we changed something in our defending with the three substitutions. "Plus it was scored by a former teammate of mine, I played with Ruben Aguilar at Monaco, and I told him I'd never seen you score a goal like that before! It was honestly a great goal." Defending champions await this weekend Como must now shift their focus back to domestic duties ahead of a challenging Serie A Matchday 11 trip to reigning Scudetto holders Inter on Sunday , November 8, prior to the international break. On the continental front, the Lariani will resume their league phase campaign by hosting AEK Athens and visiting Real Betis. Fabregas' men will then wrap up their schedule against Paris Saint-Germain before travelling to Barcelona on January 27.

item.title: Peter Obi’s Bayelsa visit triggers political realignment as Ijaw leaders demand devt, unity
item.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa The political landscape of Bayelsa State is undergoing a seismic shift following last week’s visit of Mr. Peter Obi, the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC’s presidential candidate, to the heart of the Ijaw Nation. This development, stakeholders said, has introduced a new dimension into the evolving political configuration of the state and the wider Niger Delta ahead of the 2027 general elections. Read Also: * Police arrest suspect over attack on Obi’s convoy in Calabar * LP chieftain Arabambi sues CCB over Obi’s asset declaration * Gunmen attack ADC guber candidate’s convoy in Sokoto, candidate escapes Obi’s visit, which coincided with the homecoming of Senator Henry Seriake Dickson as National Leader of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, featured the commissioning of the NDC state secretariat in Yenagoa, high-level political engagements with stakeholders, and a spectacular traditional Ijaw war canoe and boat regatta at Toru-Orua in Sagbama Local Government Area. Political analysts and Ijaw leaders who spoke to our correspondent described the developments as more than ceremonial, saying they signal the beginning of fresh political alignments and realignments that could reshape the state’s political architecture. Delivering a penetrating analysis, Professor Benjamin Okaba, a university don and immediate past President of the Ijaw National Congress, INC, said Obi’s visit “has introduced another significant dimension into the evolving political configuration of Bayelsa State and, by extension, the Ijaw Nation.” Okaba, who recalled his 2024 Bayelsa State Annual Thanksgiving remarks on political alignment and realignment, emphasized that while political affiliations may change, “our identity, history and collective aspirations as an Ijaw people must remain constant.” He said Senator Dickson’s emergence as NDC National Leader “introduces a new dimension into Bayelsa politics,” noting that his experience as a former governor and serving senator gives the party an important political foothold. However, he cautioned that “the success of any political platform must depend on its policies, credibility and commitment to the people’s welfare, not merely political structures or personalities.” Cultural Renaissance, Political Symbolism The traditional boat regatta at Toru-Orua, according to Okaba, underscored the importance of Ijaw cultural identity in political engagement. But he stressed that “celebrating our culture must go beyond ceremonial participation. Political leaders must demonstrate sustained commitment to the welfare, security and development of our riverine communities.” On Obi’s comments regarding federal attention to Bayelsa, Okaba said they “raise important questions about the marginalisation of oil-producing communities. item.title: It makes Quinnen Williams sick that Cowboys can’t stop anybody on defense

Quinnen Williams has been a major bright spot for this defense. Outside of him, though, Dallas has not had a lot of success on that side of the ball. Dallas is coming off a rather tough loss to the Arizona Cardinals. Arizona entered this game having struggled mightily on offense. They had scored 30 points in a game just once this season. He leads the team in sacks and tackles for loss by a wide margin. Despite this, he says he has to be better, and that he is not free from blame for Dallas’s defensive shortcomings. “I’m part of this defense; I’m the reason why we’ve given up touchdowns in the fourth quarter. I’m the reason why we haven’t been stopping the run as well. And I got to do better,” he said. The Cowboys have a chance to get back on track in Week 9. item.title: ‘I Will Definitely Be Your Nightmare’ – Kongthoranee, Naito Planning Intense Rematch At ONE Fight Night 49
item.description: Three-time Rajadamnern Stadium Muay Thai World Champion Kongthoranee Sor Sommai and Taiki “Silent Sniper” Naito are ready to give fans another war, this time in kickboxing at ONE Fight Night 49: Gabriel vs. Magomedov on Prime Video on Friday, November 6. Their high-stakes flyweight rematch serves as the co-main event of the U.S. primetime card in Bangkok’s legendary Lumpinee Stadium, and judging by their form, both men are primed to deliver fireworks. View this post on Instagram The Thai made a winning start to kickboxing with a unanimous decision over Yuan Pengjie at The Inner Circle 32 . Naito – hunting a fourth straight triumph – is riding the momentum of a landmark victory over previously undefeated Hyu “Mister Pepper” Iwata at ONE SAMURAI 1 . Kongthoranee won the first meeting after nine minutes of high-octane action at ONE Friday Fights 37 in October 2023, but round two is a different game, and they know it. Both men have plenty to say about it, and the Thai struck first. Kongthoranee Confident Of Repeating History Kongthoranee So Sommai already has the blueprint to beat Taiki Naito, but he is not treating it like a free pass to another spectacular victory. The 29-year-old has watched the Japanese star pile up wins since their first meeting, and he senses a sharper version waiting across the ring. That said, he remains confident that history will repeat itself. Kongthoranee told onefc.com: “Taiki has developed a lot throughout his three-fight winning streak. The main area I see him improving is his striking arsenal – that’s the dangerous part. He’s faster, heavier, and lands much more continuous combinations.” Photo Credit: ONE Championship He has never been short on answers, and his kickboxing debut proved it. The Sor Sommai man looked every bit as fluid and dangerous, picking Yuan apart round after round until the scorecards felt like a mere formality. That confidence has not made him complacent, though, and Kongthoranee knows a rematch under new rules asks different questions. The 29-year-old said: “After fighting kickboxing in my last bout, I want to develop more fluid and continuous combinations. It’ll make my strikes more effective and give me that killer instinct to finish fights. I’m confident I still have plenty of room to grow. “Facing Taiki in kickboxing does look scarier than fighting against him in Muay Thai, but I still believe I can get the job done. Here’s my message to Taiki – no matter the rules, Muay Thai or kickboxing, I will definitely be your nightmare.” View this post on Instagram With that kind of belief, the multiple-time Muay Thai World Champion is already looking beyond this guaranteed barnburner. The division’s gold sits unclaimed, and he sees a win over “Silent Sniper” as the launchpad toward it, with a seven-fight Muay Thai streak on the global stage serving as proof he knows how to build one. item.title: Not a blade of grass: USC's defense remembers its defining stand
item.description: Luke Fahey #13 of the Ohio State Buckeyes tries to evade Kameryn Crawford #1 of the USC Trojans during an NCAA football game against the on Saturday, October 31, 2026 in Los Angeles, CA. LOS ANGELES -- With a chance to take a three-score lead into halftime against Ohio State, USC running back King Miller coughed up the football. The Buckeyes recovered, took over and marched down to the Trojan one-yard line. What happened next became one of the defining sequences in their 30-18 upset: a run stuffed at the line, a false start, two incompletions and a field goal. USC went into the locker room up 20-9 instead of surrendering the momentum. Miller knew whose mistake it was. What he remembers is how quickly his teammates and coaches moved past it. "I know myself, I'm better than that," he said. "But I think the guys around me, you just got to reset. They believe in me a lot, so they just put me right back out there." Defensive end Luke Wafle, who was on the field for the stand, described it as bigger than a single goal-line stop. Two weeks after a loss at Wisconsin in which several players said teammates hadn't picked each other up properly, the sequence gave the defense the proof it was looking for. "I feel like that was a statement for us as a defense," he said. "Just not giving up a blade of grass. You just never give up." Wafle tied it directly to the trust the group has talked about all season. "You're back on your heels...how are you going to respond, and how are you going to show up for your teammate? Everybody showed up. It's all about trust." The defense earned another gift in the third quarter when linebacker Desman Stephens II punched out a fumble that eventually landed in the arms of defensive tackle Floyd Boucard. On the next play, Mark Bowman hurdled his way to a 70-yard catch. Boucard, a sophomore, credited timing and faith over skill. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect "It was really right place at the right time. I feel like God put me in the right predicament to make a play," he said. "I made a play for me and my team, and I'm really happy about that one." What stuck out to him was a sideline embrace with coach Trumain Carroll, who told him he was growing as a leader. "He just told me that I'm improving as a leader," he said. "I'm improving my body language and holding the team to the standard." That standard, Boucard and safety Christian Pierce said, has been elevated by the freshmen. Pierce said the "standard week" label for the second bye was something the team came up with this week, with help from Lincoln Riley and the leadership group, after what the Trojans learned from the first one. "Coming from our past off week, we just felt like this is how we should go about it," he said. Pierce also said the freshman class has pushed the culture in a direction that the veterans wanted. "It's impacted it a lot. Our floor had to be raised, and I feel like the guys that we brought in, they raised it on their own." Boucard said that's why

item.title: Watch Lakers’ Luka Doncic show Darius Acuff Jr. how it’s done with bonkers heater
item.description: Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Watch Lakers’ Luka Doncic show Darius Acuff Jr. how it’s done with bonkers heater appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Lakers have been largely faultless thus far this season, and arrived at the Golden 1 Center to take on the Sacramento Kings riding a 6-2 record. Luka Doncic , the points-leader in the NBA thus far this season, was once again found on a tear, and had already scored 23 points in the first half. As a matter of fact, Doncic produced 11 straight points in the second quarter, a run that pushed the Lakers to a 57-46 lead, per a post on X by ClutchPoints. It included multiple highlight-worthy moments, starting off with a trademark jumper over Leaky Black. Luka Doncic with 11-straight points in the second quarter 🔥 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) He has 23 points at halftime! pic.twitter.com/QEEYOMgeYB — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 5, 2026 He followed it up with a three-pointer over none other than Darius Acuff Jr., who has thus far endured a difficult night. The Slovenian superstar followed it up with another three, before yet another long-ranger that moved the Lakers up by 11, after the scores were tied at 46-46. Doncic, who has thus far gone 7-15 on shooting, was also helped by his partner-in-crime Austin Reaves, who had 13 points, two assists and two rebounds in the first half. The Kings, who got their first win of th season against Doncic’s previous team, the Dallas Mavericks just days ago, once again looked to Acuff Jr. for inspiration. The rookie had 19 points off 7-16 shooting, with the likes of De’Andre Hunter and Zach LaVine the other Sacramento stars to score in double digits thus far, with 14 and 11 points, respectively. The Lakers made the best of the lead their star man single-handedly snatched for them, and were leading 73-65 with more than six minutes left in the third quarter. A win will push them to 7-2 for the season, tied with the Houston Rockets for the No. 2 seed in the Western Conference. The Kings, meanwhile, will hope for a major turnaround as they look to build on their sole win of the season. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 5, 2026
item.description: The naira is trading at different rates against the US dollar across Nigeria’s official and parallel foreign exchange markets on Thursday, November 5, 2026. In the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), the dollar is valued at approximately ₦1,347.30, based on the latest reported official rate. At the parallel market, Bureau De Change (BDC) operators are buying the dollar at approximately ₦1,380 and selling at ₦1,390. The figures indicate that Nigerians buying dollars through the parallel market are paying more than those accessing foreign exchange through the official window. The difference between the official rate and the parallel market selling rate is approximately ₦42.70 per dollar. Exchange rates fluctuate depending on dollar supply, demand, market liquidity and trading activities. The parallel market rate may also vary across locations and individual currency dealers. Nigerians seeking foreign exchange for international travel, school fees, business transactions and other payments are advised to confirm prevailing rates with their banks and licensed Bureau De Change operators before completing transactions. item.title: Fragile Sharks Fall Apart in 7-2 Loss to Kings
item.description: LOS ANGELES — The San Jose Sharks visit Crypto.com Arena to take on the Los Angeles Kings. Macklin Celebrini and Ivar Stenberg scored, but the Sharks were dismantled 7-2 by the Kings. Period 1 Kempe goal: The San Jose Sharks fall asleep at the wheel. What an awful start. Gotta watch replay, but Dickinson pinched, fine, he got to the puck. But not sure what happened behind him, if there was a line change or a forward failed to cover, but Kempe got behind for the breakaway. 7 in: Multiple times, Sharks had chances to dump it in, but they lose it on entry, feeding the Kings’ counterattack. Kings have had five shots so far, not great, but even worse, all of them have felt like scoring chances or Grade-A scoring chances. I do not like what I’m watching so far. Obviously, a controlled entry is preferred to dump-in, but you must take what you’re given, too. Celebrini penalty: Another good-looking kill. I know a lot of public analytics dislike the Sharks’ penalty kill, despite their success so far. I wonder what San Jose’s internal KPI’s for their PK are? Cross-slot passes? They definitely pack up the middle, keep things to the perimeter. 8 left: Good battle between Pohlkamp and Laughton. Good test for the rookie. 7 left: Andre Lee was aggressive on the PK on Celebrini. Celebrini was surprised and lost it, little things that you don’t see as much. But seems, understandably, that PK shades toward Celebrini, and it did there. Sharks, among other things, clearly need a clear No. 2 PP option behind Celebrini. Kempe goal: Starts with not coming out together, a turnover on a Kesselring pass trying to exit. And then, coverage falls apart, how does Kempe of all people sneak into a soft spot in a defense that is sitting back in a box? This is bad. And as I was capturing this screenshot, the Kings scored another. Lots of times, it's not that you're losing, it's how you're losing. Whatever gains they might have thought that they made against Calgary, gone now. #SJSharks look rudderless pic.twitter.com/NIgaCvRtwM — Sheng Peng (@Sheng_Peng) November 5, 2026 Byfield goal: San Jose Sharks PK had done a good job of preventing high-danger chances on the kill this year, by my eye test, I know stats don’t necessarily agree. But not there. This looks like this is going to be a long road trip. Hard to keep the positivity up after that period. Sharks seem fragile right now, so fragile. Like first Kempe goal, that happens, but breakdown after breakdown, it’s could’ve been 5-0. Not calling out Natural Stat Trick, but Sharks up 1.03-0.89 in GSAx. Stats lie haha. Period 2 Misa-Celebrini-Smith, Marchment-Graf-Sherwood, Stenberg-Bystedt-Toffoli are your new lines. Celebrini goal: San Jose Sharks needed that so bad. Double-shifting Celebrini on the power play, he was with second unit there. Right move. If Celebrini healthy, as they say, I know there’s consternation about his workload, but he’s also their only way out of this. That was an unstoppable shot. Snaps six-game goalless str

item.title: 3 Candidates To Replace Jim Harbaugh With Chargers Head Coach Firmly On Hot Seat
item.description: Jim Harbaugh enters his third season as the head coach of the Chargers Getty The 2026 season has been an absolute nightmare for the Los Angeles Chargers. The team is 0-7, the offense looks completely inept under offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, quarterback Justin Herbert is having an awful season, and head coach Jim Harbaugh is having the worst year of his coaching career. Even though Harbaugh led Los Angeles to two straight 11-6 seasons and got them into the playoffs his first two seasons with the team, one cannot help but feel that Harbaugh is on the hot seat. Sure, he still has two years left on the five-year $80 million contract he signed following the 2026 season, but if it becomes obvious that he has lost the locker room and the team has quit on him then what other choice do the Chargers have than to move on? It’s important to remember that Harbaugh’s last time in the NFL ended rather abruptly after an 8-8 season with the San Francisco 49ers even though he had led the team to two NFC Championship appearances and one Super Bowl appearance in his first three seasons there. Crazy things can happen so if the Chargers continue to be absolutely awful then maybe Harbaugh will be let go and will be replaced by one of these three candidates. 3 coaches who could replace Harbaugh if he is let go Mike Tomlin It has been weird this season to watch Pittsburgh Steelers games and not see Mike Tomlin on the sideline, but his time there clearly ran its course and he had a great run which included one Super Bowl win as well as the fact that he never had a losing season. If Tomlin does want to return to coaching next season then the Chargers would have to be a pretty appetizing situation. While Herbert is struggling he has shown that he can be an elite NFL quarterback so that is one less thing Tomlin has to worry about. Tomlin runs a tight ship so if he could come in, shake things up a bit, and change the culture that could be all the Chargers need to get back on track. Kliff Kingsbury While the Chargers may be a bit gun shy on eccentric offensive-minded coaches after the disaster that the McDaniel experience has been, Kliff Kingsbury could be a high-risk, high-reward option. His tenure as head coach of the Arizona Cardinals had some highs but also plenty of lows. Maybe they need to roll the dice on someone like him. He’s currently an assistant coach for the Rams so the fact that he is working with one of the best coaches in the NFL in Sean McVay might be enough to convince the Chargers that some of that McVay magic has rubbed off on him. Nate Scheelhaase Another option on the Rams could be offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase. He’s a younger option at the age of 35 but he has worked his way up steadily through the Rams organization. He began as an offensive assistant in 2024, was promoted to pass game coordinator in 2025, and is now OC. A guy moving up like that in an organization as respected as the Rams is impressive and the fact he is offensively-min

item.title: Bears Share Malik Muhammad Injury Update as CB Trade Rumors Fly
item.description: Chicago Bears cornerback Malik Muhammad. Getty Chicago Bears dealt Malik Muhammad update before Seattle Seahawks game for Monday Night Football Getty Cornerback Nahshon Wright of the Chicago Bears. Getty The Chicago Bears already took their big swing in the trade market on Jeffery Simmons, which was an immediate home run. Most prominent NFL insiders have noted that the team’s next trip to the plate is likely to be a smaller play for a pass-rusher, such as 35-year-old Khalil Mack. However, the Bears’ injury situation in the secondary could cause a pivot to adding a cornerback over the next six days before the trade deadline. Chicago offered an injury update on fourth-round rookie cornerback Malik Muhammad on Wednesday, November 4, which was a mixed bag for the Bears. #Bears Injury Report The Chicago Bears conducted a walk-thru on Wednesday, participation is an estimation. pic.twitter.com/KYwgogbkUy — Bears Communications (@BearsPR) November 5, 2026 Muhammad sat out the team’s “Monday Night Football” showcase with a toe injury, and the Bears listed him as a limited participant in Wednesday’s practice. However, that was an estimation that Chicago offered, as the session in question was a walkthrough. Despite starting the year with a two-time Pro Bowl cornerback on one side in Jaylon Johnson and a fourth-year veteran/second-round pick in Tyrique Stevenson on the other, it has been Muhammad who has functioned as the team’s most effective cornerback through the midway point of the season. Per Pro Football Network, Muhammad boasts a 74.5 player impact score , which ranks him 58th out of 106 cornerbacks who have seen enough snaps to qualify for a rating. Meanwhile, Stevenson ranks 101st, while Johnson is second-to-last at 105th. Slot cornerback Kyler Gordon has played in just three games, so while he has been impactful, he has not seen enough snaps in 2026 to qualify for a PFN ranking. Malik Muhammad Dealing With Toe Injury, Bears Could Err on Side of Caution Given Kyle Monangai Situation Getty Chicago Bears cornerback Malik Muhammad. Toe injuries are tricky, and if Muhammad’s is a run-of-the-mill issue, he will probably return sooner than later. However, Bears running back Kyle Monangai suffered a turf toe injury in Week 4 and has sat out the last four contests since. The Bears estimated Monangai’s status as a DNP (did not practice) on Wednesday, which could mean the second-year RB sits out another game, this one against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Solider Field ahead of Chicago’s bye in Week 10. Because the Bears (6-2) have a week off following Sunday’s outing, they are liable to be more cautious with every player dealing with any type of injury concern, Muhammad included. Bears in Mix for Multiple Cornerbacks Ahead of Trade Deadline Getty Cornerback Nahshon Wright, formerly of the Chicago Bears. item.title: 'Babar Azam has the most toxic fan base': Azam Khan opens up on social media abuse in Pakistan cricket
item.description: 'Babar Azam has the most toxic fan base': Azam Khan opens up on social media abuse in Pakistan cricket originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Azam Khan has criticised the online abuse of Pakistan ace Babar Azam’s followers during a podcast. He stressed that his complaint concerned the supporters and not Babar’s ability. The host agreed, saying analysts get abusive messages even for mild, constructive criticism. 'Babar is fine, but his fan base is toxic': Azam Khan hits out at social media trolling Wicketkeeper-batter Azam Khan, who has had a fair share of online abuse himself, has taken aim at Babar Azam's fans on the Backward Point Podcast and described the fan culture around the former captain as "toxic". On virtue of being the poster boy of Pakistan cricket, Babar has been under close watch for years. Every innings he plays draws a loud reaction, and the volume of that reaction often crosses the boundaries of constructive criticism. Azam, however, was careful about where he pointed the finger. He did not say a word against Babar’s cricket, and he made it clear that his complaint was only about the behaviour of online followers. "We cricketers have a very ignorant ( Jaahil) fanbase. Obviously, nothing wrong with Babar and his game, but his fan base is very toxic,” Azam said. He then added: “I mean, if you see those things, you’d be like, ‘Bro, why would he even say that?’” MORE: 'The fittest players couldn't even chase 120': Azam Khan explodes over 2024 T20 WC scapegoating (Getty) Babar Azam’s recent form: Tri-series struggles add to his woes Babar is currently going through a lean patch of form. In the recent ODI tri-series involving Pakistan, England and Sri Lanka, the 32-year-old scored only 118 runs in five matches, at an average of 23.60 and a strike rate of 74.21. He failed to reach a half-century at any point in the competition, which has added to the worries about his recent returns in international cricket. His troubles carried over into domestic cricket, too. During the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy Gold 2026-27 match between Lahore Region Whites and FATA Region at the Diamond Cricket Ground on Wednesday, Babar was given out caught behind off Afaq Afridi on the second day of the four-day game. On the last ball of the 28th over, it appeared that Babar was beaten before wicketkeeper Rehan Afridi collected it. The bowler appealed at once, and the on-field umpire raised his finger. Babar looked unhappy with the decision and pointed towards his thigh pad, apparently to suggest that the ball had hit the pad and not the bat. He nevertheless walked off after making 28 off 40 balls, an innings that included six boundaries. MORE: India and Pakistan could face each other upto 10 times in the upcoming year Why Azam Khan’s remarks on Babar Azam’s fan base deserve to be taken seriously Azam Khan deserves credit for choosing his words with care. It would have been easy to turn the convers

item.title: Bruins’ 4th-Line Energy Winger Making Noise In Providence
item.description: ANAHEIM, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 19: Michael Eyssimont #81 of the Boston Bruins controls the puck during the second period of a game against the Anaheim Ducks at Honda Center on November 19, 2025 in Anaheim, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) Getty Michael (Mikey) Eyssimont is having a great month. Providence Bruins fans have probably noticed his name showing up on the scoresheet pretty often. And there’s a good reason. Like the Boston Bruins, he is red hot to start the season. Eyssimont finished October with 10 goals and three assists in 10 games. That’s quite a stretch for any player, and it was good enough to earn him AHL Player of the Month honours. Tuesday night stat check 📈⤵️Mikey Eyssimont leads the league with 10 goals in 7 games played, helping the forward earn AHL Player of the Month honors for October. 🔥 pic.twitter.com/rBIRIQxS0H — Providence Bruins (@AHLBruins) November 4, 2026 The goals weren’t all on quiet, one-goal nights, either. Eyssimont had five multi-point games during the month and scored two hat tricks. He put three past the Charlotte Checkers in a 6-2 Providence win on October 10. Then he did it again eight days later, scoring three times in a 6-1 win over the Hershey Bears . When a player puts together a month like that, people take notice. What’s interesting is that the Bruins weren’t exactly having a great October as a team. They finished the month 4-6-0-0, scoring 30 goals and allowing 30. Providence struggled, but Eyssimont did his part to keep the offence moving. He was involved in 13 of those 30 goals. That’s a pretty big share of the team’s scoring. He’s Been Around the Block Eyssimont isn’t some young player trying to figure out professional hockey. He’s already spent a good deal of time in the NHL and knows what it takes to play at that level. Last season, he appeared in 56 games with Boston, scoring eight goals and adding 10 assists. Over his NHL career, he’s played 269 games, with 33 goals and 41 assists. He’s also familiar with the AHL. Before this season, his last full stretch at that level was in 2022-23. He has played 236 career AHL games, recording 61 goals and 69 assists. So he’s bringing quite a bit of experience to Providence. He’s been in NHL dressing rooms, played against some of the best players in the game, and now he’s back in the AHL making a real difference. It’s always interesting to see how a player with that kind of background handles a return to the minors. So far, Eyssimont seems to be enjoying himself. What’s Next for Eyssimont and Providence? The Bruins could certainly use more nights like the ones Eyssimont has been putting together. They got November off to a terrific start with an 8-0 win over the Lehigh Valley Phantoms. That’s a nice way to get a new month going after a fairly uneven October. Of course, nobody expects Eyssimont to score 10 goals every month. That’s a pretty tall order. But if he keeps producing, he’ll give Providence a much better chance of turning things

item.title: Emiliano Martínez back in training with Chelsea
item.description: COBHAM, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 4: Emiliano Martínez of Chelsea during a training session at Chelsea Training Ground on November 4, 2026 in Cobham, United Kingdom. (Photo by Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC via Getty Images) | Chelsea FC via Getty Images Emiliano Martínez, looking like he just had a fight with his wisdom teeth and lost really badly at the dentist, was back in Chelsea training yesterday , less than three weeks after suffering a fractured jaw in our 2-0 win against Everton. Our first-choice goalkeeper had to have emergency surgery after being stretchered off the pitch on Merseyside, but it seems like he could be back in action far sooner than anyone could’ve reasonably expected — if not with Chelsea then with Argentina, who called him up for international duty this week as well. (The November international break begins after this weekend’s matches.) In Martínez’s absence, young Mike Penders has stepped up and with good effect overall, despite that massive blunder against Spurs on his full debut. Presumably he’s going to cede his starting spot back to Martínez, though whether that happens this weekend against Sunderland or just after the international break, remains to be seen. Martínez’s teammate at both club and international level, Aarón Anselmino also returned to training yesterday after recent injuries (and the youngster was also called up to Argentina), and Jordan Henderson looked to be back to 100 per cent after dealing with an illness last weekend. In less good news, Moisés Caicedo was not spotted in the open portion of yesterday’s training. Hopefully it’s nothing serious. Last time this happened, Reece James had to have surgery. Emiliano Martinez, Jordan Henderson and Aaron Anselmino involved in #ChelseaFC training this morning. Moises Caicedo not present for first 15 minutes open to @SkySportsNews cameras. Still no Maxence Lacroix, Joao Pedro or Reece James. #CFC pic.twitter.com/msvEjNoo2u — James Savundra (@JamesSavundra) November 4, 2026

item.title: The Kennel Has a Job to Do This Weekend With Four-Star Recruit Jalen Davis Visiting
item.description: ATHENS, GREECE - MAY 21: Jalen Davis, #07 of U18 Next Gen Team 3SSB and Kristupas Sabeckas, #01 of U18 Zalgiris Kaunas in action during ANGE Finals Round 1 U18 Zalgiris Kaunas vs U18 Next Gen Team 3SSB at Sunel Arena on May 21, 2026 in Athens, Greece. (Photo by David Grau/Euroleague Basketball via Getty Images) The Gonzaga Bulldogs have just a lone commit out of the 2027 recruiting class: four-star Dooney Johnson. The 6-7 point guard, originally hailing from Milwaukee Juneau, Wisconsin, will play his senior high school season with East River in Orlando, Florida. Another high-level backcourt talent from the Class of 2027 is four-star combo guard Jalen Davis, who recently named the Zags as one of his top-four schools, along with the Washington Huskies, UCLA Bruins, and North Carolina Tar Heels. He doesn’t have a commitment date yet. NEWS: 2027 Top-25 overall recruit Jalen Davis is down to four schools, he told @Rivals : ⁰⁰Gonzaga, North Carolina, UCLA, and Washington⁰⁰The 6-foot-3 senior is one of the top guards in the 2027 class. https://t.co/Za8P3EM19D pic.twitter.com/IiprrPopn4 — Joe Tipton (@JoeTipton) November 3, 2026 The 6-3 prospect from Bremerton, Washington, will take an official visit to campus in Spokane, Washington, on Nov. 7 for Gonzaga’s 2026-27 home opener against the Conference USA’s New Mexico State Aggies. Davis has already taken official visits to Washington on Sept. 27, North Carolina on Oct. 3, and UCLA on Oct. 13. The 18-year-old, high-volume scorer plays mostly off-ball, but can make an impact in the passing lanes. During his standout junior high school season, Davis was awarded the state of Washington’s Gatorade Player of the Year honor with averages of 31.5 points on 63.9 field goal percentage and 40.0 three-point percentage, 9.6 rebounds, 5.2 assists, and a whopping 5.8 steals per contest for Bremerton High School. He won back-to-back WIAA Class 2A state championships in 2025 and 2026 there, looking for his third in a row to cap his senior campaign. An in-state commitment out of Kitsap County on the western part of Washington to pair alongside Johnson would change the perspective of what this Inland Northwest program can look like for at least the next two seasons, maybe more. The Kennel does a fantastic job making those visiting recruits feel at home, chanting their names. But Davis is a much larger fish, and the students have to be at their loudest in order to convince him to make the McCarthey Athletic Center his permanent home. It helps that this weekend’s matchup is the first home game of 2026-27 and the crowd’s first true chance to see this current group of Zags in action. The energy is going to be at its highest, even against a mid-major program in the non-conference that not many would be interested in watching. Arden Cravalho is a Gonzaga University graduate from the Bay Area… Follow him on X @a_cravalho

item.title: Norwayne uses second half scoring bonanza to top Mansfield Christian
item.description: MANSFIELD - Two years ago Peyton Zollinger and his Norwayne teammates got a taste of regional tournament action losing in a shootout to Beachwood in the semifinals. Wednesday evening at Ashland Community Stadium, the Bobcats found themselves back in a regional semifinal against Mansfield Christian and made program history in a 5-1 win advancing to their first regional championship. "We have worked for this for four years," Zollinger said. "I dressed as a sophomore when we lost in regional semifinals ... this year we're graduating a lot of seniors, so it was the year." DIVISION III: Mansfield Senior unlucky in regional semifinal loss In miserable conditions with sideways steady rain and intermittent downpours, the Bobcats controlled the first half but could not break down the Flames' defense. And just before halftime, it was Mansfield Christian who found a breakthrough on a lobbed through ball that skipped on the turf and over the defense where Jacoby Dickinson was able to latch onto it and slot past Norwayne's Garrett Ponting with 41 seconds to go in the half. "We spent too long settling into the game," Mansfield Christian coach Kaedon Anderson said. "When we did, we started playing our style of soccer and had a lot of success. There was a lot of confidence coming into the second half and we anticipated to start the second half the way we finished the first. We made a few defensive adjustments in anticipation for them." What the Flames couldn't anticipate was the tenacity the Bobcats opened the second half with. A shot from Lysander Bauman deflected off a Mansfield Christian player and out for a corner kick with 32:20 on the clock. Up steps Zollinger who proceeds to score an olimpico directly from the corner in the 49th minute to bring the teams level. "I knew when I hit it that someone was getting it or I was scoring it," Zollinger said. "I felt the wind in the air, hit it, and it went in." Over the next 11 minutes, though, it would go from an even match to a commanding three-goal lead for Norwayne as Bauman buried a cross into the back of the net followed by Zollinger's second on a nearly 40-yard free kick, then Bauman laid off a ball to Erik Neruda who hit it on the half-volley past Mansfield Christian's Joshua Hillman in goal. "We anticipated them to start the second half that way ... and I think some unfortunate calls (affected us)," Anderson said. "A corner given to them that we thought went the other way, and they score off it. A foul we didn't think was a foul, they score off it. Things like those are game-changing moments and we're a young team ... you can't expect them to be held to a standard of how you manage those moments when they've never been in them. "But four goals in 11 minutes kills your morale." Five goals in 16 minutes was irrecoverable as Sintay Maibach iced the match with exactly 15:00 on the clock for the Bobcats' final goal of the night. "We were able to pin them and really get up the field ... and we told them the guys

item.title: Virginia Tech football vs SMU: Preview, odds, how to watch
item.description: DALLAS, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Kevin Jennings #7 of the SMU Mustangs celebrates a touchdown during the first half against the California Golden Bears at Gerald J. Ford Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. (Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Virginia Tech Hokies head back on the road this week for an important Friday night ACC clash against the SMU Mustangs in Dallas. It’s a battle between a pair of 6-2 teams, with the Mustangs holding a 4-2 mark in ACC play, while the Hokies are 3-2. SMU was ranked 19th last week, before going on the road and being shocked by Syracuse, 30-27. Meanwhile, Virginia Tech is coming off a bye week after going on the road two weeks ago and picking up a massive win at Clemson. It’s one of the most important wins for the Hokies in years. Quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer found tight end Luke Reynolds on fourth down with under two minutes remaining for the go-ahead touchdown. Then, Brent Pry’s defense shut the door on a Clemson comeback. Here’s a closer look at this week’s game between the Mustangs and Hokies. 3 Mustangs to know QB Kevin Jennings : They don’t come more experienced than Kevin Jennings. He’s played in 47 games for SMU, including 34 starts. Jennings has also helped SMU win a lot of games. He’s a career 67% passer with 88 total touchdowns. He also doesn’t turn the ball over a lot. Jennings has also taken better care of the football this season. While Jennings is a passer first, he’s the type of quarterback who has given Virginia Tech fits with his legs. RB Kendrick Raphael : The senior running back is playing for his third ACC team (NC State, Cal, SMU). He’s having a terrific season, with 692 rushing yards and 9 touchdowns. Virginia Tech coach James Franklin shared his concerns about Raphael earlier this week. Obvously, the Hokies would prefer to slow down Raphael without bringing extra bodies in the box, because that only makes Jennings more dangerous as a passer. DE Marques White : Franklin is concerned about SMU’s front with its size and athleticism. The Hokies are expected to get two veteran offensive linemen back for Friday’s game, which should help. Marques White is the name to watch. He leads the Mustangs with 5.5 sacks. SMU has two 300-pounders in the middle of the defensive line who can move, which will be a problem for VT’s offensive line. 3 keys to victory Make Jennings earn every yard : Franklin said it best. The Hokies need to make Jennings go through his progressions, that means a solid pass rush and good coverage on the back end. If the Hokies can’t get pressure on Jennings, he could have a big day. SMU has 7 players with 14 or more receptions, 9 players with 111 or more receiving yards. This is a dangerous offense. It all begins with Jennings. Run the ball : Too often this season, the Hokies have struggled to get the run going. They have the backs, with Jeff Overton and Marcellous Hawkins. item.title: Rockford Guilford set to host the IHSA Boys State Soccer Tournament
item.description: ROCKFORD, Ill. (WTVO/WQRF) — Some IHSA boys state soccer champions will be crowned this weekend in Rockford at Swanson Stadium.
