item.title: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander inches closer to Kevin Durant’s Thunder record after Cavs beatdown
item.description: Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images Shai Gilgeous-Alexander inches closer to Kevin Durant’s Thunder record after Cavs beatdown appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Shai Gilgeous-Alexander once again demonstrated why he remains one of the NBA’s most dominant players. The Oklahoma City Thunder superstar put together an exceptional performance to guide the Thunder to a 124-116 win over the Cleveland Cavaliers despite OKC dealing with several injury concerns . The back-to-back MVP finished the win with 42 points, five rebounds and eight assists. He went 11-of-26 from the field, 5-of-11 from beyond the arc and 15-of-19 from the free-throw line. It marked his second consecutive 40-point performance after he scored 43 points in the previous game against the Cavs. With this impressive outing, Gilgeous-Alexander adds another significant achievement to his legacy in Oklahoma City. The Thunder superstar continues to close the gap on franchise greats Kevin Durant and Russell Westbrook in the team’s all-time 40-point games ranking. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Meanwhile, only two players have managed to record 40-point performances in consecutive games this season. Luka Dončić has accomplished the feat twice, while Gilgeous-Alexander has done it once. Gilgeous-Alexander has been putting together another remarkable run this season, averaging 30.1 points, 4.3 rebounds, 4.5 assists and 2.3 combined steals and blocks per game. He is shooting 45% from the field, 36% from beyond the arc and 85% from the free-throw line. The Thunder guard is now averaging at least 30 points per game for the fifth consecutive season. The Thunder were once again without three key starters: Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren and Cason Wallace . However, despite missing several important players, they managed to get enough production from their available roster to secure another crucial victory. While Gilgeous-Alexander grabbed most of the attention, Oklahoma City also benefited from valuable contributions from its supporting cast. Ajay Mitchell delivered an impressive performance, finishing with 23 points to give the Thunder another dependable scoring option. Rookie Bennett Stirtz also stepped up, putting together a a career-high 16 points. The Thunder will now aim to maintain their winning momentum when they face the Memphis Grizzlies in their next matchup on Friday. item.title: 2027: APC flags off Enugu campaign in Nsukka, vows to deliver Mbah, Tinubu, other candidates
item.description: …Governor highlights projects, promises more roads, jobs, infrastructure …Charges electorate to sweep away opposition with their votes The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Enugu State on Wednesday officially flagged off its campaign for the 2027 general elections, with party leaders and stakeholders pledging to mobilise voters across the state for the re-election of Governor Peter Mbah and President Bola Tinubu. The campaign flag-off, which held at Nsukka Township Stadium, witnessed a large turnout of party faithful, political office holders, traditional and community leaders, as well as supporters from across the three senatorial districts. Speakers at the event described the mammoth crowd as a demonstration of the APC’s political strength in Enugu State, insisting that the party was determined to consolidate its presence and secure victory for all its candidates in the forthcoming elections. Addressing the gathering, Governor Mbah highlighted his administration’s investments in security, infrastructure, education, healthcare, economic development, and revival of moribund assets and completion of abandoned projects. He urged the people to assess his government’s performance through its achievements and ongoing projects, noting that the opposition had not even presented any manifesto. Reflecting on his journey to Nsukka ahead of the rally, Mbah said the ongoing dualisation of the Penoks–T-Junction – Ugwogo-Opi-Nsukka road had significantly reduced travel time and improved safety. “I left the office a few minutes past 1pm. It took me two to three minutes to get to T-Junction from Penoks. And it just reminded me of how motorists could have spent so much time, sometimes up to 30 minutes or hours if we did not dualise that road. “From T-Junction all the way to Nsukka, I noticed that work was going on right left, green, what have you. The contractor assured me that a realistic commissioning date is before the end of this year. “Another thing the road reminds me is that we have kissed empty Mondays goodbye. Once upon a time, we dreaded traveling on that road because of fear of attack are gone. Today, we have kissed it goodbye,” he stated. According to him, the administration’s infrastructure programme is not merely about constructing roads, but also about reconnecting communities, expanding economic opportunities and promoting greater integration across the state. He cited the 40km Owo-Ubahu-Amankanu-Umualor-Ikem virgin dual carriageway, which connects to Obollo-Afor road as another intervention designed to improve connectivity, and now links communities in the northern part of the state, while also serving as a new gateway to the North Central part of the country. On education, Mbah said the Smart Green Schools initiative was fundamentally designed to transform the quality of learning and prepare children for a productive future and modern economy. item.title: Justin Herbert reacts to opponent saying he’s ‘seeing ghosts’
item.description: Nov 1, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert (10) at press conference after the game against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Chargers are still searching for their first win of the season, and quarterback Justin Herbert has been at the center of their struggles. After Sunday’s 24-9 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, one of the players who intercepted him didn’t hold back. Rams safety Quentin Lake said that Herbert was “seeing ghosts” in the game, adding that he was “throwing deli meat out there.” It was a brutal critique of a quarterback who is supposed to be the face of the franchise. On Wednesday, both Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh and Herbert himself were asked about Lake’s comments. Needless to say, Harbaugh did not see things the same way. Chargers’ Winless Start Sunday’s loss dropped the Chargers to 0-7, making them the only winless team left in the NFL. It’s the franchise’s worst start since 2000. Herbert completed 24 of his 32 passes for 257 yards against the Rams, but he didn’t throw a touchdown and was intercepted twice. Lake picked him off on a short pass early in the game and returned it 45 yards, setting up a Rams field goal, and Trent McDuffie later added a second interception. The Chargers’ offense has been a mess all season. They have scored just 99 points through seven games, and they haven’t found the end zone in their last nine quarters. Herbert, meanwhile, has thrown at least one interception in every game this season. ‘Seeing ghosts’ Lake appeared on the St. Brown Podcast after the game and offered a blunt assessment of Herbert’s performance. “He was throwing deli meat out there,” Lake said, via the St. Brown Podcast . “He’s seeing ghosts. I don’t know what’s going on, but we knew we were gonna get a couple. At least one.” Harbaugh, however, pushed back on that critique when asked about it on Wednesday. “As far as anybody’s opinion I don’t see that,” Harbaugh told reporters . “Everybody’s entitled to their opinion. Not what I see.” He actually thought Herbert played well against the Rams. “I thought he played — did his job exceptionally well,” Harbaugh said. “You know, two throws he would have liked to have back.” Herbert, for his part, claimed that he hadn’t even heard about Lake’s comments. “I haven’t looked into it, haven’t heard anything about it, so I can’t really make a comment about it,” Herbert told reporters . “We’re really just focused on what’s going on in the building, playing football and doing what we can and doing our best to, you know, go put our best effort out on Sunday. And that’s all that really matters. Anything outside of that is out of our control.” The post Justin Herbert reacts to opponent saying he’s ‘seeing ghosts’ appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Spurs’ Victor Wembanyama makes NBA history with eye-popping first half stats vs. Mavericks
item.description: Credit: Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images Spurs’ Victor Wembanyama makes NBA history with eye-popping first half stats vs. Mavericks appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . There are nights when San Antonio Spurs star Victor Wembanyama makes the game of basketball look so easy. Wednesday night is one of those nights. In a matchup against the Dallas Mavericks, Wembanyama had his way in the first half — racking up insane stats that have him making history. Through the first 24 minutes of game time, Wembanyama put up an eye-popping 29 points, 15 rebounds, and five blocks to go along with two assists and two steals. In so doing, the Spurs star became just the first player in NBA history to record at least 25 points, 15 rebounds, and five blocks in a single half, as per Jordan Howenstine of Spurs PR. In a matchup between two of the most talented first-overall picks in the past five seasons, Wembanyama is showing that he is miles ahead of Cooper Flagg. The Spurs star simply had his way with the Mavericks, and San Antonio held a 17-point lead heading into the halftime interval as a result of this domination. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) If Wembanyama were to end the game with the stat line he put up in the first half on Wednesday, that would already be a good game for him. But he has an entire half to do more damage against the Mavs, and it will be interesting to monitor how much more eye-popping his stats on the night could be. It’s not like the Mavericks have poor big-men defenders on their roster. They have Daniel Gafford, who is a respectable paint protector, while Flagg and PJ Washington are also stout defenders in their own right. There seems to be something with the Mavericks that brings the best out of Wembanyama . Last season, he had 40 points in the Spurs’ season-opening win in Dallas, and he averaged 31.3 points courtesy of two 40-point outings against the Mavs. Perhaps Wembanyama is well and truly leaning into that Texas rivalry. item.title: Player grades: SGA's 42 points lead Thunder to 124-116 win over Cavaliers
item.description: OKLAHOMA CITY — Dribbling the ball between his legs, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander stared down his next victim. As Tyrese Proctor was left alone on an island, the two-time MVP vindicated his outside-happy shot diet. He drilled a stepback 3-pointer that sealed another momentum-building night in their new NBA reality. The Oklahoma City Thunder came out with ample energy in a 124-116 win over the Cleveland Cavaliers . They're slowly relearning how to play without Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace. Super-sizing the starting lineup, the Thunder absolutely ran the Cavaliers out of the gym from the jump. Kenrich Williams knocked down an outside jumper. He slashed to the rim. The ball ping-ponged around as Alex Caruso's return from a three-game absence was met with roaring applause. It didn't take long for the Thunder to put up some wacky scores. At one point, it was 25-9. And then 30-15. They had a 37-20 lead after the first quarter. Pretty surreal to see them completely out-energize Donovan Mitchell and James Harden. The onslaught continued in the second frame. At one point, the Thunder doubled up the Cavaliers on the scoreboard, 50-25. The second unit kept the momentum going as the Cavaliers looked half-asleep and ready to get out of town in their sole trip to OKC of the year. The Thunder had 23 points in the second frame. They entered halftime with a 60-44 lead over the Cavaliers. Coming out of the halftime break, the Cavaliers tried to make up ground quickly. They rattled off the first nine points of the second half. Harden drained an outside jumper through contact. And then Mitchell went coast-to-coast for a fastbreak layup. Once OKC saw its lead fall to single-digit points, Gilgeous-Alexander quit with the trolling shot diet of pull-up 3-pointers. He returned to his bread and butter. Overall, the Thunder rebounded well. They had 28 points in the third quarter. That kept them a healthy distance from the Cavaliers with an 88-74 lead. For the most part, OKC stiff-armed Cleveland on the scoreboard. Micah Peavy has provided a jolt of defensive energy. So did Caruso — per usual. After Caruso fed Aday Mara a dump-off pass for a cutting dunk, that felt like the punctuation mark. The Thunder had a 111-93 lead with a little under four minutes to go. Of course, the Cavaliers made a fake hot run. Mitchell tried his best Tracy McGrady impersonation by knocking down unconscious deep jumpers. Alas, all that did was extent the game by about a dozen minutes. Also helped Gilgeous-Alexander cross 40 points for a second consecutive game. The Thunder had 36 points in the fourth quarter. That was just enough to keep up with Cleveland's high-scoring 42 points in the final frame. Needing a morale boost. OKC's two-game sweep over the Cavaliers has brought most of the fanbase back into the cautiously optimistic side of things. The Thunder shot 46% from the field and went 15-of-36 (41.7%) from 3. They shot 27-of-35 on free throws. They had 25 assists on 41 baskets.

item.title: Tim Hardaway Sr. calls out Giannis Antetokounmpo while praising Cooper Flagg
item.description: Tim Hardaway Sr. calls out Giannis Antetokounmpo while praising Cooper Flagg originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Miami Heat have not been off to a great start as expected in the 2026-27 NBA season. After trading for Giannis Antetokounmpo, the Heat were supposed to be competitive to the highest level. Unfortunately, they have struggled, as they had a 2-5 record heading into Wednesday's game against the Los Angeles Clippers . While Giannis has been playing well, the rest of the team has struggled. Tim Hardaway Sr. prefers Cooper Flagg over Giannis Antetokounmpo The Heat have been an interesting team to follow because before the season, there was considerable hype behind them. Their defensive potential was quite high because of Giannis, Bam Adebayo, Andrew Wiggins, and Davion Mitchell. Unfortunately, the Heat have struggled on both ends of the floor. Despite the hype around them, they have not performed well based on expectations, and they are seen as one of the biggest disappointments early in the season. MORE: Dwyane Wade gets brutally honest about Bam Adebayo's Miami Heat role Heat legend Tim Hardaway Sr. has watched the games because he loves the franchise and his son plays for the team. However, it seems that he wants to be brutally honest about his opinion on Antetokounmpo and how he prefers the Dallas Mavericks ' star in the making, Cooper Flagg. "He’s better skilled about running offense. At seeing the floor, a better handle, a better jump-shot, he has a better understanding of the game," Hardaway said on the Crossover podcast . Alongside his criticism of Antetokounmpo, Hardaway also did talk about the Heat's poor mindset on both ends of the floor. While the Gianis take might be bold, Hardaway is making some valid points that they can improve on moving forward. item.title: APC has mechanism to manage our govs, Rainbow Coalition’s feud — Yilwatda
item.description: *We’ve no plan to make Nigeria one party state *Nigerians should choose leaders based on records, character, capacity to deliver *Says Tinubu’s reforms must translate into jobs, food, better incomes, security By Soni Daniel, Northern Regional Editor National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Prof. Nentawe Goshwe Yilwatda, has said the ruling party has no ambition to turn Nigeria into a one-party state despite the influx of politicians from opposition parties into its fold. Yilwatda, who spoke on the 2027 general elections, governance and the APC’s preparations for the polls, said a strong ruling party and a competitive multiparty democracy could coexist. In an interview with Vanguard, the APC chairman also said the party had mechanisms to resolve differences between some APC governors and the Federal Capital Territory Minister, Nyesom Wike’s Rainbow Coalition, insisting that internal disagreements would not derail its preparations for the elections. He defended President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, saying the administration had established measures to reposition the economy but must now translate them into jobs, affordable food, better incomes and improved security. Yilwatda urged Nigerians to assess candidates on their records, character and capacity to deliver rather than allow political differences to dictate their choices. As a democrat, are you not worried that the mass exodus of other politicians into the ruling APC can create a one-party state if the APC wins in January next year? I am a democrat, and I believe that Nigeria’s democracy is stronger when political parties are vibrant, competitive and able to offer citizens credible alternatives. The APC does not seek to eliminate opposition, nor do we believe that a healthy democracy can be sustained without it. The movement of politicians from one party to another is a feature of democratic politics. Individuals make such decisions for different reasons, and every Nigerian has the constitutional right to freedom of association. What matters is that these movements are voluntary and conducted in accordance with the law. However, the responsibility for maintaining a competitive political environment does not rest with the APC alone. Opposition parties must also strengthen their internal structures, build public confidence, articulate credible policies and organise effectively. Our ambition is not to turn Nigeria into a one-party state. Our ambition is to build a party that Nigerians freely choose because of its leadership, programmes and record of performance. A strong APC and a competitive multiparty democracy are not mutually exclusive. We will continue to respect the rights of other parties to organise, campaign and seek the people’s mandate. How is the APC under your leadership helping to actualise the dream of progressive politics, which seeks to make life better for all and reduce authoritarianism? item.title: ‘How BVN exposed fake Amnesty beneficiaries’
item.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA—The Presidential Amnesty Programme, PAP, has said its insistence on the Federal Government’s Bank Verification Number, BVN, policy has exposed fake beneficiaries and fraudsters feeding off the programme. The office, while condemning what it described as blackmail and campaign of calumny against its administrator, Dr. Dennis Otuaro, by some misguided elements from the Niger Delta, said it would not succumb to blackmail and will not sideline the BVN policy designed to link all bank accounts belonging to individuals and eradicate corruption. “The PAP office cannot be the exception in the execution of the government’s policy on BVN designed to eradicate corruption in the society,” the Office said in a statement, yesterday, Mr. Igoniko Oduma, Special Assistant on Media to the Administrator, said. “Clearly, anybody using the tool of blackmail to arm-twist the office to sideline BVN is either a criminal or a fraudster, who should be under security watch. The Office has asked them to come for verification of their claims, but they will not. “These serial blackmailers are purveyors of falsehood and hollow narratives; they are driven by sheer greed with the sole objective of denting Dr. Otuaro’s image and distracting him from focusing on the task given to him by President Bola Tinubu. “These misguided elements are angry with Dr. Otuaro for prudent management of resources, and introducing reforms that have sanitised the PAP. Many of them are angered by what is statutorily paid to them by the Office. Some want to be awarded bogus contracts which, the office under Otuaro, is not inclined to do.” The programme said rather than divert funds to satisfy blackmailers, resources are being deployed efficiently for lasting peace and security in the Niger Delta, with tangible results including 13,300 onshore and over 500 offshore scholarships, distribution of laptops to beneficiaries, and prompt payment of ex-agitators’ monthly stipends. It listed other achievements as employment of four cadet pilots and 20 aviation trainees after training, on-the-job training for 40 cadets, professional certification for 98 maritime cadets, and training of over 360 stakeholders on alternative dispute resolution and mediation. Vanguard News The post ‘How BVN exposed fake Amnesty beneficiaries’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: State Police: Kano, Cross River, Abia, Niger, Benue, Oyo yet to approve bill; gets Nov 19 deadline
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA—THERE are strong indications that the National Assembly is prepared to transmit the State Police Bill to President Bola Tinubu for assent as thirty states have so far approved the bill. The proposed State Police system has crossed a major constitutional hurdle, with 30 State Houses of Assembly approving the amendment required to pave the way for its establishment. This leaves six states yet to submit approved bill to the National Assembly for onward transmission to the President for subsequent assent. The six states that have not approved the bill are Kano, Cross River, Abia, Niger, Benue and Oyo. The Senate has, however, given them up till November 15 to do so, warning that failure to respond by the deadline could be deemed as withholding approval. The six states are expected to communicate their decisions before November 15, when the National Assembly intends to forward the proposed constitutional amendment to President Bola Tinubu for subsequent. Disclosing these while updating lawmakers on the progress of consultations with the 36 state legislatures on the proposed amendment yesterday, the Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, APC, Ekiti Central, said the number of approvals had exceeded the constitutionally required two-thirds of the 36 state legislatures. According to him, for the process to be rounded off, it has to be in three phases, with the National Assembly expected to pass the bill; the approval by at least two-thirds of the state legislature; and the President to sign the bill into law. He added that the National Assembly had fulfilled its responsibility by passing the bill and transmitting it to all 36 State Houses of Assembly for consideration and approval. Bamidele said: “Let me explain again, for the avoidance of doubt, three keywords are used in the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999, as amended. The first word is passage, the second word is approval and the third assent. “The reason the writers of our Constitution, our forefathers, put all these specific words is to ensure that no part of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria can be easily amended without the buying in of all the critical stakeholders at all levels of governance. “The passage of the bill was the responsibility of the National Assembly, and that has been completed. Approval is required from at least two-thirds of the 36 State Houses of Assembly in the country, while assent must subsequently be given by the President to complete the constitutional amendment process.’’ He explained that the constitutional requirements were deliberately designed to ensure that amendments to the nation’s supreme law enjoyed the participation and agreement of critical stakeholders across the different levels of government. Bamidele stressed that the 30 approvals already received were significantly above the constitutional requirement of 24 states, describing the development as evidence of widespread support for the proposed ref

item.title: Voter register: INEC to purge 1.5m irregular registrants
item.description: •Amupitan can’t supervise credible polls in 2027 — Ezekwesili By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA—The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, is set to delete about 1.5 million voter registrations found to be irregular from the national register, ahead of the 2027 general elections. This is even as former Education Minister, Oby Ezekwesili, said yesterday that Nigeria could not conduct a credible 2027 election under an Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, led by Prof. Joash Amupitan. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, disclosed this while receiving a delegation on a courtesy visit to the commission’s headquarters in Abuja yesterday. The delegation was led by the Special Representative of the United Nations Secretary-General for West Africa and the Sahel and Head of the United Nations Office for West Africa and the Sahel, UNOWAS, Mr. Leonardo Santos Simão. Amupitan said technology-enabled verification helped the commission isolate the affected entries. The deletions, he explained, were part of a comprehensive cleaning of the register through the claims and objections process. The final register is scheduled for publication on December 15, 2026. Amupitan said the commission had registered approximately 103 million voters, with young Nigerians, aged 18 to 34, making up nearly 29 per cent of them. Amupitan said INEC would continue to strengthen the use of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS, for accreditation, and the INEC Result Viewing Portal, IreV, for public access to polling-unit results. He said the commission was also planning a mock accreditation and election to test these tools, identify possible challenges and build public confidence before the 2027 polls. Amupitan identified misinformation, disinformation and foreign information manipulation as major threats to electoral integrity. He warned that the growing misuse of Artificial Intelligence, AI, and coordinated online campaigns could undermine public confidence in the electoral system. INEC under Amupitan can’t supervise credible polls in 2027, says Ezekwesili Meanwhile, former Education Minister, Oby Ezekwesili, has said Nigeria cannot conduct a credible 2027 election under an Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, led by Prof. Joash Amupitan. According to her, INEC has lost all credibility to be an independent umpire of Nigeria’s elections. Oby, who spoke against the backdrop of allegations of corruption involving the voter register through the use of artificial intelligence, noted that INEC’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Dr Lawrence Bayode, on October 30, 2026, told Nigerians that INEC registration officers purportedly used their official login credentials to inject AI-generated photographs, duplicate records and other fabricated entries into the preliminary register of voters. item.title: APOD: 2026 November 5 – Enceladus in Silhouette
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 5 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Enceladus in Silhouette Explanation: One of our Solar System’s most tantalizing worlds, Enceladus is backlit by the Sun in this Cassini spacecraft image from November 1, 2009. The dramatic illumination reveals the plumes that continuously spew into space from the south pole of Saturn’s 500 kilometer diameter moon . Discovered by Cassini in 2005, the icy plumes are likely connected to an ocean beneath the ice shell of Enceladus. They supply material directly to Saturn’s outer, tenuous E ring and make the surface of Enceladus as reflective as snow. Across the scene, Saturn’s icy rings scatter sunlight toward Cassini’s cameras. Beyond the rings (lower right), the night side of 80 kilometer diameter moon Pandora is faintly lit by Saturnlight . Tomorrow’s picture: pixels in space Date: November 5, 2026 Credit: Cassini Imaging Team , SSI , JPL , ESA , NASA Authors & editors: Jerry Bonnell, Cecilia Chirenti, Robert Nemiroff, Keighley Rockcliffe A service of: ASD at NASA / GSFC , NASA Science Activation & Michigan Tech. item.title: Flamingos beat Brazil to reach first U17 Women World Cup final
item.description: Nigeria’s U17 women’s team, the Flamingos, have reached the final of the FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup for the first time in history after defeating Brazil 3-1 in the semi-final. The Flamingos secured the historic victory with goals from Queen Joseph and Awawu Bashiru, who scored twice. Joseph opened the scoring in the 56th minute before Bashiru extended Nigeria’s lead in the 71st minute. Bashiru completed her brace in the 80th minute to seal Nigeria’s 3-1 victory and book their place in the final. The achievement marks a major milestone for the Nigerian side, who won bronze at the 2022 edition of the competition. The Flamingos will now face Japan in the final as they seek to win their first-ever FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup title. item.title: Cyprus: Island of Snakes, Cats, and Ophiolites
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Cyprus: Island of Snakes,… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search Seasonal rains had started to fill Akrotiri Salt Lake when the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 8 captured this image of Cyprus’s Akrotiri Peninsula on October 10, 2026. NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison The island of Cyprus began to form some 90 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous , with molten rock pouring from the seafloor, solidifying, and building new oceanic crust . Over time, portions of this oceanic rock were wrenched upward by tectonic forces , eventually emerging as a rugged island made of ophiolite , a type of rock with a mottled green appearance said to look like the skin of a snake. Remnants of that ancient island are still visible in the dark rocks of the Troodos Mountains . During the Miocene , considerably younger layers of chalk, limestone, marl, and other marine sedimentary rocks accumulated around the island, providing material that developed into a second, smaller island to the south during a later period of geologic uplift . Over time, sediment poured from rivers into the channel separating the two islands and combined with marine sediments to create deltas and eventually two land bridges, or tombolos . The joined landmass comprises the Akrotiri Peninsula , now the southernmost tip of Cyprus. The sandy edges of the peninsula were visible when Landsat 8 captured these images on October 10, 2026. Akrotiri Salt Lake , a coastal lagoon that was once an arm of the Mediterranean Sea, lies between the two tombolos. The more westerly feature, the Kouris River tombolo, formed first, developing about 50,000 years ago from river-deposited gravels and sands. The eastern tombolo extended southward from Cyprus, cutting off the Mediterranean Sea only within the past 2,000 years, according to geologists . The lake’s water levels now vary markedly with the seasons, typically filling in the late autumn and winter and drying out in the summer. The influx of winter water has historically attracted sizable overwintering flamingo populations, averaging about 4,000 birds. However, the wintering flamingo population has declined in recent years, plummeting to 30 birds in 2025, according to news reports . Flamingos have long flocked to the lake to feed on fairy shrimp , which are rich in colorful substances called carotenoids that give the birds their famously pink hue . Snakes are another of the island’s more notorious animal inhabitants. In antiquity, Cyprus was known as Ophiousa , or “ land of snakes ,” likely due to its robust population of blunt-nosed vipers . item.title: FG records N4.69trn fiscal deficit in Q1’26 as revenue falls
item.description: •Nigeria’s economy grows 3.89% – Budget Office By Udeme Akpan The Federal Government (FG) recorded an aggregate fiscal deficit of N4.69 trillion in the first quarter of 2026, as revenue generation fell significantly below target, highlighting challenges in financing the 2026 budget. This came as Nigeria’s economy grew by 3.89 per cent in real terms during the quarter, driven by improved performance in the oil and non-oil sectors. Figures from the Budget Office of the Federation (BOF), contained in its 2026 Budget Performance Report, showed that the fiscal deficit was N4.69 trillion, compared with the prorated target of N7.86 trillion for the January–March period, representing N3.18 trillion below projection. The report showed that aggregate Federal Government revenue stood at N5.08 trillion, compared with the quarterly target of N9.22 trillion, resulting in a shortfall of N4.14 trillion. This represented about 55 per cent of projected revenue. Similarly, aggregate government expenditure amounted to N9.76 trillion, against the projected N17.08 trillion, indicating an underperformance of N7.32 trillion, or about 57.2 per cent of the target. On deficit financing, domestic borrowing stood at N3.9 trillion, compared with the prorated target of N4.61 trillion, leaving a shortfall of N704.03 billion. However, foreign borrowing, projected at N2.70 trillion for the quarter, recorded no actual inflow during the period. The Federal Government also realised N287.44 billion from multilateral and bilateral project-tied loans, against the quarterly target of N512.23 billion, while privatisation proceeds stood at N3.32 billion, compared with the projected N47.29 billion. The figures highlight the government’s difficulties in generating sufficient revenue and accessing planned financing sources to support budget implementation. Nigeria’s economy grows 3.89% On economic performance, the Budget Office reported that the oil sector grew by 2.57 per cent year-on-year in real terms during the first quarter, up by 0.70 percentage points from 1.87 per cent recorded in the corresponding period of 2025. The non-oil sector expanded by 3.94 per cent, outperforming the oil sector and accounting for a larger share of the economy’s growth. The Budget Office described the performance as “a period of macroeconomic stabilisation accompanied by moderate real-sector expansion.” However, it identified weak, although improving, revenue performance as a major constraint to budget execution, noting that the Federal Government continued to meet its non-discretionary expenditure obligations. It stated: “Improving revenue collections in the subsequent quarters of the year is critical to the successful execution of the 2026 Budget.” The report said the government would intensify efforts to improve economic growth and revenue generation, while controlling recurrent expenditure, particularly personnel costs. item.title: Police arrest suspect over attack on Obi’s convoy in Calabar
item.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Cross River State Police Command on Wednesday arrested a 27-year-old man, Victor Edet Yellow Duke, in connection with an attack on the convoy of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Peter Obi, in Calabar, the state capital. The attack left the windshields of some vehicles smashed. The incident occurred at about 2:20 p.m. at the Watt Market Roundabout as the convoy was returning from the palace of the Obong of Calabar to Metropolitan Hotel, the venue of the party’s presidential town hall meeting. According to the police, a group of suspected hoodlums, reportedly armed with machetes and sticks, emerged from the Calabar Road and Clerks Alley axis and attacked vehicles in the convoy. The number of vehicles affected had not been ascertained. Police personnel deployed in the area moved in swiftly to contain the situation. Their intervention, which included the use of tear gas, led to the arrest of the suspect, while the other attackers fled. The suspect was later taken to the State Police Headquarters by operatives of the Violent Crime Response Unit, VCRU, for what the command described as a discreet investigation, to prevent reprisals or a further breakdown of law and order. Normalcy has since returned to the area. In a statement by its Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Sunday Eitokpah, the command said the Commissioner of Police, CP Ajo Geoffrey Ordue, had ordered a thorough investigation to identify and arrest other participants and establish the full circumstances of the incident. Cautioning against presuming the suspect’s guilt, the police said: “The arrest of a suspect does not amount to a determination of guilt, as the suspect remains entitled to the presumption of innocence pending the conclusion of investigation and any subsequent judicial proceedings.” The command assured residents, political stakeholders and visitors that adequate security measures remained in place across the state. It reiterated its commitment to “providing equal security protection to all political parties, candidates and their supporters, irrespective of political affiliation.” It also urged the public to stay calm, avoid spreading unverified information and report suspicious activities through established police channels. Eitokpah added: “The Cross River State Police Command remains committed to maintaining public safety, protecting democratic participation and ensuring that all lawful political activities are conducted in a peaceful and secure environment.” The post Police arrest suspect over attack on Obi’s convoy in Calabar appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: US Midterms: Implications of democrats’ victory
item.description: PRESIDENT Donald Trump has acknowledged the impact of the United States’ attack on Iran and a sharp rise in gasoline prices on stunning Republican losses in midterm elections, but said the move was justified and denied responsibility for the rout. The Democrats won both the US Senate and House of Representatives, taking control of Congress for the rest of Donald Trump’s presidency. The tally showed that Democrats grabbed 54 and 234 seats at press time to win the Senate and House of Representatives respectively. Historic firsts The election also delivered some historic firsts with the Democrats flipping at least seven Senate seats in ruby-red states and battlegrounds like Kansas, which hasn’t elected a Democratic senator in nearly a century, Iowa, Texas, Ohio, Maine, North Carolina and South Carolina. They held on to battleground seats in Georgia and Michigan. In the the House, Democrats would start the year with what would be its largest majority in nearly two decades, NBC News projects. Democrats flipped more than two dozen districts, some that voted for Trump by double digits in 2024. In the gubernatorial races, Democrats also flipped GOP-held offices: Keisha Lance Bottoms in Georgia, Amy Acton in Ohio, Rob Sand in Iowa, Gina Hinojosa in Texas and Aaron Ford in Nevada. Specifically, David Crowley, Democrat, has become the first Black governor in U.S history, Abdul El-Sayed becomes the first Muslim ever elected to the U.S. Senate, James Talarico becomes the first Democrat elected in Texas since 1988, Xavier Becerra becomes the first Latino elected governor in California history, Gina Hinojosa becomes the first Latina elected governor in Texas history, while Deb Haaland becomes the first Native American woman elected governor in U.S. History. I’m willing to accept results, work with Democrats – Trump Reacting to the election defeat, Trump said he was willing to accept the results of the midterm elections and work with Democrats as they made gains across the country. “We’ll, you know, look forward to working with them,” he told The New York Times shortly before 10:30 p.m. while watching results come in. “We’ll probably work something out.” Trump said Democrats had reached out to him about working together and that he thought they could find common ground on the debt ceiling. He added that he has “total veto power, so they have to come to us.” In a preview of his likely governing style over the next two years, Trump also posted a picture of his trademark red cap emblazoned with the word “veto” to convey his determination to block legislation carried by the incoming Democratic-controlled Congress. And the gasoline was caused by Iran,” he told Fox News in a televised phone interview late on Tuesday. “People agree with what I’m doing on Iran, but they really probably weren’t

item.title: Atiku breaks through in Sokoto
item.description: By Abubakar Auwal, Salim Ashir Mahuta, Sokoto & Mumini Abdulkareem, Ilorin The African Democratic Congress (ADC) finally held its presidential campaign flag-off in Sokoto on Wednesday after uncertainty over the venue of the rally and whether the party would be allowed to hold the event in the state. The event was largely peaceful, but some party supporters were alleged to have come under attack en route to the campaign ground, with two persons reportedly shot. Analysts say the flag-off represents a breakthrough for the opposition, as the atmosphere had been dominated by the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), which began its campaign on October 24, in Kaduna. The ADC campaign flag-off was held against the backdrop of hostility the party faced preparatory to the event, including the takeover of hotel accommodation allegedly by the state government, the sealing of its party secretariat and refusal to grant the use of public squares for the event. Even as at late Tuesday night, few hours to the D-Day, it wasn’t clear if the rally was going to take place as the presidential candidate of the party, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar and his running mate, Rotimi Amaechi; the national chairman of the party, Senator David Mark and other members of the party were yet to arrive at the state. By early Wednesday morning, things began to shape up when the party scaled over a major hurdle and secured a venue for the rally. The ADC announced on Wednesday, that its state secretariat along Ilorin Road, Sokoto, would serve as the venue for the presidential campaign flag-off. It was then the party announced that Atiku and other national leaders of the party were expected to arrive in Sokoto at 9am through the Sultan Abubakar III International Airport. The announcement cleared the air over the controversy which came with conflicting reports on where the event would be held. Our correspondents report that supporters of the ADC turned Atiku’s arrival into a carnival as they intensified their call for a change of government, repeatedly chanting “Tinubu Must Go”. The slogan rang out at the Sultan Abubakar III International Airport, Sokoto, where party supporters gathered to welcome Atiku and his entourage, with members of the Tinubu Must Go Movement leading the chant. Atiku and his entourage arrived in Sokoto at about 1 pm but did not reach the ADC State Secretariat, the venue of the campaign rally, until around 4:30 pm, following the large crowd that turned out to welcome them. The journey from the airport to the city centre would ordinarily take no more than 15 minutes. The triple-lane airport road was filled with ADC supporters waving party flags and displaying campaign posters and banners of the party’s candidates. Many sang, danced and celebrated along the route. The campaign venue was also filled to capacity, with some supporters climbing onto the roof of the party’s four-storey secretariat. item.title: Weak labour movement ‘ll hurt all, not just workers – NLC
item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young The consequences of a weakened labour movement could extend far beyond factories, government offices and other workplaces, leaving millions of Nigerians without a strong collective voice to challenge policies affecting their economic survival, rights and welfare. Read Also: N70,000 Transport Allowance Saga: ‘You can’t lead TUC from abroad,’ Ajaero tells Osifo For the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), the strength of organised labour is not just a trade union concern but a matter that directly affects the wellbeing of the entire country. Beyond its traditional responsibility of negotiating wages and protecting workers’ interests, Labour movement has historically served as an important platform for defending ordinary Nigerians, challenging unpopular government policies and protecting the civic space. Its weakening, therefore, could have consequences for people who are not necessarily members of any trade union but whose livelihoods are affected by government decisions. This was the concern expressed by the President of the NLC, Joe Ajaero, who warned that Nigerians would become victims if the labour movement collapsed. “If the labour movement collapses today, all of us will become victims,” Ajaero declared in Lagos, while speaking at the 2026 Annual Conference of the Labour Writers Association of Nigeria (LAWAN), themed: Workers at the Centre of Nigeria’s Political Transition: Defending Rights, Advancing Welfare and Building Economic Justice. His warning was particularly directed at Nigerians who appear to regard the struggles of organised labour as the exclusive responsibility of workers and trade union leaders, even when the issues being contested affect their daily lives. According to him, the labour movement remains one of the important voices defending the interests of ordinary Nigerians, adding that its collapse would leave workers and other vulnerable groups with fewer platforms through which to express their grievances. He said: “If that voice becomes weak, workers and other vulnerable groups will have fewer platforms through which to express their grievances.” For Ajaero, the danger is that a weakened labour movement would not only affect the ability of workers to negotiate better conditions of service but could also reduce the capacity of ordinary citizens to collectively challenge economic policies that worsen their living conditions. He questioned the attitude of Nigerians who complain about the rising cost of living but expect the NLC to take responsibility for confronting every challenge without corresponding public support. “It is not enough to complain about the cost of fuel, transportation, food or other necessities and then ask where the NLC is,” he said. “The labour movement cannot solve every problem without the participation and support of the people.” The NLC president argued that the struggle for affordable living conditions should not be left to organised labour alone because the consequences of economic

item.title: Amidst heatwave, electricity supply shortage bites harder
item.description: From Abdullateef Aliyu, Mohammed Musbau and Dotun Omisakin, Lagos; Yusuf Akogu and Idris Bature (Abuja); Hamisu Kabir Matazu, Maiduguri; Ahmad Datti, Kano and Promise Adagba The worsening electricity supply situation across several parts of the country has heightened the hardship residents face amid the recent heatwave, Daily Trust reports. From Lagos to Abuja, Kano, Maiduguri, Ondo State, Kwara, and other states, residents have lamented declining electricity supply, with some reporting outages lasting days or weeks. The situation has forced many households to adopt uncomfortable and, in some cases, risky measures to survive the heat, while businesses dependent on electricity are counting their losses. In Lagos, the frustration over persistent blackouts recently spilled onto the streets as residents of Lagos Island staged a protest, demanding an immediate restoration of electricity to their communities. The demonstration, which took place on Tuesday, involved mainly women from Lewis, Okesuna, Beecroft, Simpson and Sandgrouse streets, who expressed anger over prolonged power outages and the discomfort caused by rising temperatures. They called on the electricity distribution company to address their plight. The residents said the absence of electricity had compounded the discomfort caused by intense heat, leaving households struggling to sleep, preserve food and carry out daily activities. The situation has been attributed in some areas to constraints in power generation and reduced electricity allocation from the national grid. In August, Eko Electricity Distribution Company (EKEDC) reportedly said its allocation had fallen from 486 megawatts to 347 megawatts, forcing it to adjust electricity supply to some feeders. The latest demonstration also followed a warning by the Lagos State Government about the possibility of extreme heat as the dry season approaches and the El Niño climate pattern strengthens. Following the El Nino weather pattern, it has been projected that Nigeria could record an additional 31,400 heat-related deaths between September 2026 and February 2027. The projection by the Climate Impact Lab places Nigeria among the countries expected to suffer the highest number of additional heat-related deaths globally during the six-month period of El Niño, with nearly half of the 66,800 deaths projected across the Sahel region expected to occur in the country. However, the combination of high temperatures and unreliable electricity has heightened residents’ concerns, especially over their ability to keep homes comfortable and businesses operating. The situation is no different on Lagos Mainland, where residents have been without electricity supply for the past few days. The Ikeja Electricity Distribution Company, which serves the Lagos Mainland and some parts of Ogun State, has been sending apologies to the residents over the blackout. item.title: Destruction of campaign posters, billboards: Police read riot act to politicians, thugs, miscreants
item.description: *IGP orders Police Commissioners to arrest, prosecute offenders *Avert Obi, Kwankwaso /APC supporters clash in Calabar By Kingsley Omonobi & Ike Uchechukwu ABUJA — Force headquarters yesterday warned politicians, thugs, miscreants and other persons with affiliations to members of the political class responsible for destruction of campaign posters, billboards and banners belonging to candidates and parties to desist or face prosecution. The warning came against the backdrop of persistent complaints by political parties and their candidates about how thugs allegedly sponsored by their opponents had continuously destroyed their campaign materials, making it impossible to market themselves to the electorate. This came on a day Police and other security operatives prevented a possible violent clash in Calabar, Cross River State,between hundreds of supporters of Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso and a large group of All Progressives Congress, APC, supporters on campaign walk. Giving the warning yesterday, Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Aniete Iniedu, said in a statement that those who chose to break the law will face the full consequences of their actions. The statement read: “The Nigeria Police Force has observed with serious concern the growing incidents of deliberate tearing, defacement and destruction of political campaign posters, banners and billboards belonging to candidates and political parties across the country ahead of the 2027 general elections. “The Force strongly condemns this act of political intolerance and warns political thugs, hoodlums and other mischief-makers involved to desist immediately. “For the avoidance of doubt, destroying, defacing or unlawfully removing another candidate’s campaign posters and billboards may constitute malicious damage, which is a criminal offence under applicable criminal laws (Section 451 of the Criminal Code Act and Section 326 of the Penal Code Law which defines the offence of mischief). ‘Political differences or loyalty to a particular party do not give anyone the right to destroy another candidate’s property or infringe on their right to campaign freely. “The Force reiterates that all political parties and candidates, irrespective of their affiliation or status, are entitled to equal protection under the law. “No individual or group has the right to determine whose campaign materials should be displayed or destroyed. IGP orders CPs to action “The Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Disu, has directed commissioners of police across the 36 states of the federation and the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, to take proactive measures to prevent such acts. ‘’He ordered investigation of reported incidents to ensure that persons found culpable are arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the law. ‘Political sponsors and individuals who recruit, encourage or facilitate these criminal acts will equally be held accountable where evidence establishes their involvement. “The Force calls on political part

item.title: Senate proposes six-month jail term for hospitals denying emergency care
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate has passed for second reading a bill seeking to make it compulsory for public and private hospitals across Nigeria to provide emergency medical treatment, prescribing up to six months’ imprisonment for facilities and individuals who violate its provisions. The proposed legislation also prescribes a fine of up to ₦300,000, imprisonment for six months, or both, for anyone convicted of denying emergency medical treatment. The bill, sponsored by Senator Abdulaziz Musa Yar’Adua (APC, Katsina Central), seeks to amend the National Health Act, 2014, to establish mandatory emergency medical treatment standards and referral protocols in healthcare facilities. Titled, “A Bill for an Act to Amend the National Health Act, 2014 to Provide for Emergency Medical Treatment Standards and Referral Protocols in Healthcare Facilities; and for Related Matters, 2026” (SB. 759), it was referred to the Senate Committee on Health (Secondary and Tertiary) for further legislative action, with a directive to report back in four weeks. Under the proposed amendment, no healthcare provider, health worker or medical establishment would be allowed to deny anyone emergency medical treatment for any reason. It also requires healthcare professionals to commence life-saving interventions, including cardiopulmonary resuscitation, airway management and bleeding control, immediately after identifying a life-threatening condition. The bill proposes that hospitals conduct triage and initial assessments within 15 minutes of a patient’s arrival, while basic stabilisation measures, including oxygen administration, intravenous fluids, pain management and initial diagnostic procedures, must begin within 30 minutes. For patients requiring admission, hospital beds are to be assigned within two hours, subject to availability. Where beds are unavailable, healthcare facilities would be required to commence immediate stabilisation and arrange the patient’s transfer to another hospital. The proposed legislation further requires hospitals to initiate referral arrangements within two hours and complete the transfer process within three hours of a patient’s arrival, except where circumstances beyond their control prevent compliance. It also mandates hospitals to dispatch an ambulance or arrange alternative transportation within 30 minutes of communicating a referral decision. Beyond emergency response timelines, the bill seeks to introduce mandatory emergency care training and certification for healthcare workers, with recertification intervals not exceeding 18 months. It also mandates the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria and the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria to jointly develop a standardised national emergency care curriculum. However, healthcare practitioners would be protected from penalties where resource constraints prevent compliance, provided the challenges are properly documented and prescribed referral procedures are followed. item.title: Duty & Allegiance: Gowon’s memoirs, an exercise in self-justification! By Olu Fasan
item.description: In the Acknowledgements section of his recently published memoirs My Life of Duty & Allegiance, General Yakubu Gowon, a former military head of state, writes: “Let me begin by saying that I was not anxious to document my memoirs, but the calls for me to do so kept coming.” Well, I am one of those who kept urging General Gowon to write his memoirs. I did so in three interventions in this column, the last of which, in March last year, was daringly titled “A plea to General Gowon: Sir, write your memoir before you die!” (Vanguard, March 13, 2025). So, when Gowon published his memoirs in May this year, I did not hesitate to spend £29.98 (about N54,000) to buy a copy from Amazon. I read the 760-page book with great interest! First, congratulations are in order! General Gowon truly deserves commendation for writing such a historically significant book. His was the last voice everyone wanted to hear on the most epochal events in the annals of this country: the 1966 coups and civil war, during which he was head of state. Gowon addresses those thorny issues in the memoirs, a masterpiece. The book starts with General Gowon’s removal from power in July 1975. Chapter 1, titled “Our Boys Are Up To Something”, deals with the coup that toppled him while he was attending a summit of the then Organisation of African Union, OAU, in Kampala, Uganda. This is instructive because the memoirs, divided into 36 chapters, are almost entirely Gowon’s ripostes to various allegations and criticisms against him. He leaves virtually no allegation or criticism unaddressed. And on each, he admits no wrong, no fault, no error! It was entirely an exercise in self-justification, without a single mea culpa! It is impossible to discuss Gowon’s comprehensive memoirs in one column, and I won’t do so here. In other columns, I would address the quality of governance and the public service ethos under General Gowon’s regime, as well as the 1966 coups and the civil war. In the present intervention, however, my focus is on what I regard as the memoirs’ general flaws, one being its somewhat weak evidential base. Reading the book, it struck me that, in some places, much of what General Gowon says is based on conjectures, insinuations and assertions. Of course, unlike an autobiography, which requires research, dates and facts, a memoir is usually based on memory and subjective interpretation. Nevertheless, the recounting of significant events in Nigeria’s past by one of its key dramatis personae should not be devoid of historical accuracy. To be fair, General Gowon explains the paucity of evidence, saying: “I want to emphasise that I am telling my story without access to my crucial personal records, since many important documents taken from my desk after my removal in July 1975 were discarded by those who succeeded me.” Of course, in doing so, those people denude Nigeria’s historical narrative of richness. The documents that survived, Gowon says, “were destroyed by two serial fire incidents.”

item.title: Uber says it alone can make robotaxis pay, hours after Waymo quit its app
item.description: Google-owned autonomous cab company Waymo has revealed it will stop allowing Uber users to book its robo-cabs, hours before the OG rideshare giant made a case for all autonomous vehicle fleet operators to use its platform instead of creating their own. This slow-motion fender bender played out across Wednesday, starting with Waymo Co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana telling Bloomberg that her company would end a partnership that saw it work exclusively with Uber in Austin and Atlanta. Mawakana said Waymo wasn’t happy about the fact that when users of Uber’s app requested a ride in one of its robo-cabs, they weren’t guaranteed to get one. News of that break-up came on the same day that Uber announced its quarterly results. As is common on such occasions, the company published remarks [PDF] its execs intend to make during an earnings call. CEO Dara Khosrowshahi used those remarks to promote the idea that Uber is the natural home for robotaxi fleet operators, because it already delivers around 30 percent higher trips per vehicle per day compared to apps run by autonomous cab companies. He said that higher utilization rate, plus use of shared charging and maintenance infrastructure, can deliver “higher fleet profitability even after paying Uber’s marketplace fee.” “As autonomous technology becomes more widely available, we believe this ability to commercialize vehicles profitably will become an increasingly important source of competitive advantage and value capture.” The two events are deliciously ironic, because Uber is arguing the scale of its platform makes it the ideal host for third-party players – just as Google does with its search, app store, and YouTube services. Left unsaid is that the two companies hold concerningly dominant positions in their respective markets. Khosrowshahi also outlined more ways Uber intends to strengthen its position, including by putting around 2,000 robo-cabs on the road in 2027, before “a much larger commercial ramp beginning in 2028.” That plan means Uber will run some cars itself and rely on third-party robo-cab operators who allow bookings on its app. “Importantly, building a broad ecosystem does not mean spreading our resources evenly,” the CEO explained. “We intend to maintain an open platform while concentrating capital, integration resources, and hands-on deployment support behind a smaller group of partners with the clearest paths to commercial scale and attractive economics at maturity.” Or in other words, as Uber uses more robo-cabs, it will try to maximize profits. Uber users booked $59.8 billion worth of services in its third quarter, up 20 percent year-over-year. The company recognized $14.75 billion of that as revenue, a ten percent improvement. Rideshare accounted for $29.5 billion of bookings and $7.5 billion of revenue. Delivery services brought in $5.5 billion of revenue on $28.5 billion of bookings. No wonder Khosrowshahi wants more robo-cabs: they’ll boost Uber’s more lucrative business. The company might

item.title: American Bitcoin (ABTC) Posts $126 Million Profit as Holdings Gain $197 Million
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine American Bitcoin (ABTC) Posts $126 Million Profit as Holdings Gain $197 Million American Bitcoin Corp. (Nasdaq: ABTC) reported about $126 million in third-quarter net income on Wednesday, a swing from a $57.2 million loss in the prior quarter that rested largely on a $197.3 million gain on the company’s bitcoin holdings rather than on mining revenue. The Miami-based miner and treasury company, a majority-owned subsidiary of Hut 8 Corp. and co-founded with Trump family backing, mined about 891 bitcoin in the quarter at a cost of roughly $42,100 each and ended September with about 8,427 BTC. Mining revenue was about $63.4 million, down from about $67.0 million in the second quarter. Gross profit was about $25.8 million, a 41% margin, compared with about $33.0 million and 49% a quarter earlier, as seasonal power costs rose across its sites. Adjusted EBITDA came in at about $221 million, compared with an Adjusted EBITDA loss of about $45.0 million in the second quarter, according to the company’s release . Eric Trump, co-founder and chief strategy officer of American Bitcoin, said the quarter delivered the net income and Adjusted EBITDA figures while growing the bitcoin reserve and bitcoin per share. Chief Executive Mike Ho said the company kept mining at a structural discount to spot and raised satoshis per share by about 5% without issuing shares through its at-the-market program or buying bitcoin on the open market. A paper gain carried American Bitcoin’s quarter The income statement makes the driver plain. American Bitcoin booked a $197.3 million gain on digital assets in the third quarter, after a $71.2 million loss on that line in the second. Operating income was about $191.8 million. Other expense included a $64.3 million loss on derivatives. Strip the mark-to-market move out of the picture and the operating story looks quieter. Revenue per bitcoin mined was about $71,100, down slightly from about $71,900 in the second quarter, and the cost to mine rose to about $42,100 from about $36,500, the company said. Production of about 891 bitcoin was below the second quarter’s roughly 932 coins, which the company had called its highest quarterly haul on record when it reported a $57.2 million second-quarter loss alongside a climb in holdings to about 8,002 BTC. American Bitcoin said it sold a portion of production to cover operating costs while still adding to its strategic reserve. Holdings rose by about 425 bitcoin, or about 5%, to roughly 8,427 as of Sept. 30. That total includes about 3,090 bitcoin pledged for miner purchases under agreements with Bitmain. Reserve up, satoshis per share up Management’s preferred yardstick is satoshis per share, which rose about 5% to roughly 11,572 from about 10,989 at the end of June. The share count reflects a 1-for-15 reverse stock split effected earlier this year on July 2. The owned fleet stood at about 89,242 bitcoin miners with roughly 28.1 EH/s of capacity at quarter-end. item.title: NASA Announces X-70 Experimental Aircraft to Advance Flight Research
item.description: Generated image of NASA’s new X-70 Fractal experimental aircraft, a crewed, rapidly reconfigurable research platform for advanced aviation technologies. On Wednesday, NASA unveiled its newest experimental aircraft, the X-70 Fractal, during the UP.Summit at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. This high-performance, highly adaptable research platform is designed to accelerate the development and testing of advanced aviation technologies. The crewed X-70 features advanced, rapidly reconfigurable flight-control technology that will allow NASA to explore aircraft maneuverability in ways never before demonstrated in crewed flight. The aircraft can also accommodate up to 2,000 pounds of experimental payloads in internal and external locations, enabling a wide range of research and flight-testing opportunities. “The X-70 Fractal gives NASA a crewed, high-performance platform to test advanced flight-control, maneuverability, and other cutting-edge technologies in real flight,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “Its modular design and ability to rapidly swap internal and external payloads will keep our teams flying, learning, and moving quickly from one experiment to the next. We expect her first flight under the NASA banner within the next two years, and X-70 is just one part of this new beginning for aeronautics. This is why people come to NASA: to build, to learn, and most importantly, to fly.” The X-70 Fractal has a takeoff weight of 10,000 pounds and is designed to cruise at Mach .75, reach altitudes of up to 45,000 feet, and provide an operational range exceeding about 1,726 miles (1,500 nautical miles). These capabilities will enable NASA to conduct demanding flight research across a broad range of operating conditions. “For decades, NASA Aeronautics has used X-planes to develop technologies that advance aviation,” said Laurie Grindle, director of the Aeronautics Division within NASA’s Research and Technology Mission Directorate. “It’s exciting to bring on another X-plane to accelerate and drive aeronautics research.” The X-70 joins a storied legacy of experimental aircraft that have helped establish America’s leadership in aviation. From the Bell X-1, which first broke the sound barrier in 1947, to the X-15 hypersonic research aircraft and today’s X-59 quiet supersonic demonstrator, NASA has spent decades pushing the boundaries of flight. With the X-70, NASA will expand its capacity to conduct experimental flight research, accelerate the testing of emerging technologies, and advance the next generation of American aviation. For more information about NASA’s aeronautics research, visit: https://www.nasa.gov/aeronautics -end- George Alderman / Cheryl Warner Headquarters, Washington 202-358-1600 george.a.alderman@nasa.gov / cheryl.m.warner@nasa.gov Share Details Last Updated Nov 04, 2026 Editor Jennifer M. Dooren Location NASA Headquarters Related Terms Aeronautics Flight Innovation NASA Aircraft Research and Technology Mission Directo

item.title: Meta brings Conductor on board its model train
item.description: Meta has acquired AI coding startup Conductor, signaling interest in applying AI to software engineering tasks. Charlie Holtz, the startup's co-founder and CEO, made the announcement in a blog post . He also revealed that the company's hosted Conductor Cloud, a sandbox for hosted agents, will go read-only on November 13 and shut down on November 20. Conductor , the eponymous company's macOS app for running multiple coding agents simultaneously in isolated copies of Git projects, will continue working for the next few months, and the biz expects to provide a way to transfer Conductor Cloud workspaces to local machines. But in early 2027, Conductor will no longer receive new models or critical bug fixes. A Meta spokesperson confirmed that the acquisition will strengthen the company's developer-oriented AI capabilities but declined to elaborate further. Perhaps Conductor will play nicely with Muse Code , Meta's recently introduced coding agent. Having spent heavily on strengthening its AI research lab , Meta has moderated its appetite for big acquisitions since April when China blocked its $2 billion offer for Manus AI , a developer of software agents. Meta's other acquisitions this year, Moltbook , Assured Robot Intelligence, and Stilla, are also AI-oriented but more modest in scope. The Conductor deal comes without an announced price, and follows in the footsteps of Meta regaining credibility as a model provider : Llama 4 disappointed but Meta's recent Muse Wonder and Spark models rank respectably among the top LLMs at the moment. In Meta's most recent conference call for investors [PDF], CEO Mark Zuckerberg said his company aims to provide AI agents that non-technical people can deploy for business tasks. "What we see is a lot of people are actually using Muse today to help run especially small businesses," he said. "And we think that there's both an opportunity to help create an agent that people use to really enable them to automate and do a lot of the parts of spinning up a small business that are just kind of difficult and time-consuming but aren't the core thing that a person is trying to do." Meta's AI strategy, as Zuckerberg describes it, is focused on collecting transaction fees from businesses for enabling agentic commerce, selling advanced AI capabilities to developers in the form of model access or tokens, charging for Muse to automate business tasks, and applying AI to personalize and improve results from ads. It's a good time to run an AI-related startup, as leading model companies seek to add value beyond offering AI models. Models themselves have become commoditized to the point that only a few leading model makers can get away with charging a premium. In an effort to maintain that lead, top model makers have been purchasing innovation (and talent) while they are still flush with investor funds. item.title: Building AI factories at enterprise scale
item.description: AI has become a juggernaut, driving technical strategy in the tech sector and outside of it. With the worldwide server market growing 30 percent in a single year to hit $122.6bn in the first quarter of 2025, IDC now feels safe recategorizing AI-driven investment "from cyclical to durable". The analyst company expects inference to account for over 70 percent of computing demand by next year, adding that it's growing fastest at the edge. Why enterprises are building their own All this investment in AI infrastructure might once have come mainly for hyperscalers, but that's changing quickly. Adoption is spreading quickly beyond public cloud service providers into enterprise environments, IDC adds. They're eager to run agentic AI in-house. There are plenty of reasons for companies to own their own AI infrastructure rather than offloading it to the cloud. One of these is data control, especially in regulated sectors such as finance, healthcare, manufacturing, and the public sector that have sovereign data requirements. Another revolves around the need for predictable costing from tokens delivered on tunable in-house systems. So what should companies look for in a supplier? Delivery speed will be a powerful driver for many who are under the gun to deliver AI initiatives for the business, especially during periods of constrained memory and CPU supply. Life cycle services will also come near the top of the list, for companies that need help managing everything from the power through to the reasoning LLM models and the workloads that use them. That need for expertise is unlikely to stop; companies will undergo changes in AI strategy as they get to grips with a still-evolving technology. From the desk to the datacenter ASUS expects this AI surge to continue in the datacenter, but elsewhere too, specifically in edge locations (especially industrial use cases) and at developers' desks, as the applications that will power the enterprise get made. It wants to be top of peoples' list for hardware and services at all these places along the AI continuum. At NVIDIA's GTC show in Berlin on Oct 21-22, it announced a full-stack AI offering that it's calling its Enterprise Agentic AI Solution . It's three-layer affair, featuring: ASUS AI Server and Infrastructure: Its selection of AI servers, including several new units. ASUS AI Software Stack: Its software for integrating and controlling AI workflows. ASUS AI HUB: A services operation that ties it all together. These bring together some existing assets that ASUS had for enterprise AI users, along with some new ones. The time is right for an end-to-end offering with new hardware because of the way the market is shifting, say ASUS execs. "ASUS servers help enterprises build high-performance agentic AI infrastructure capable of supporting both complex task execution and large-scale AI agent deployment, accelerating enterprise adoption of agentic AI," says Paul Ju, senior vice president and head of infrastructure solution

item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 4, 2015: A rail-launched Super Strypi rocket carrying 13 baby satellites failed during its debut launch for the US Air Force
item.description: null On Nov. 4, 2015, the United States Air Force planned to launch an experimental rocket for small satellites from the Pacific Missile Range Facility off Barking Sands, Kauai, Hawaii. The launch didn't according to plan . For this mission, the Air Force was testing out the Super Strypi rocket . The rocket used a rail to help with the liftoff. Super Strypi left the ground, but the rocket quickly spun out of control. When it crashed, it destroyed all of the tiny satellites riding aboard the rocket. The cause? Likely a problem with the first stage motor. The mission lost 13 tiny satellites known as cubesats. Cubesats are a popular option for space missions, because they are small and cheap, and they often operate in swarms. After failing to launch this batch of cubesats, the Super Strypi program never recovered from its failure, and the Air Force never tried launching another one. The U.S. Air Force’s rail-launched Super Strypi rocket lifted off from Hawaii about 9:45 p.m. local time on Nov. 3, 2015,, roared toward the sky and failed less than a minute into the long-awaited flight. (Image credit: U.S. Air Force) Why it mattered The Super Strypi rocket was a 21st century take on a 1960s rocket. It was designed to be a modern version of the three-stage Strypi sounding rocket used for for reentry vehicle and anti-missile target tests. Its three stages, powered by Aerojet Rocketdyne solid rocket motors, was designed to reach orbit, rather than suborbital trajectories common to most sounding rockets. The U.S. Air Force hoped Super Strypi would be a new tool for quick-response launches based on national security needs. Altogether, it was designed to launch small payloads of up to 300 kilograms into space for a mere $15 million per mission . The rocket's primary payload was the ORS-4 satellite, short for Operationally Responsive Space 4, which was built for the Air Force by engineers at the University of Hawaii (who nicknamed it HiakaSat). It was designed to capture Earth imagery and monitor the environment over the course of a year. The 12 other payloads on Super Strypi included eight cubesats for NASA's Edison Demonstration of Smallsat Networks mission, and as well as four others for universities that had been added as secondary payloads. Since the Super Strypi failure, neither the Air Force or Space Force has opted to use the rocket for a new mission. The Space Force has turned instead to commercial companies for fast-turnaround launch support. In June of this year, the U.S. Space Force teamed up with Rocket Lab to launch the Victus Haze mission with just 17 hours of notice , a new record to demonstrate short-turnaround launch response.

item.title: Nintendo's biggest ROM chip supplier is bowing out of the business
item.description: For years, the AI industry's insatiable demand for memory and storage has had plenty of knock-on effects on the price and availability of PC components like RAM , SSDs , and GPUs . Now those shortages are also squeezing the supply of ROM chips that power physical Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 game cartridges. Chip manufacturer Macronix announced in its third-quarter earnings report that the company's production of ROM chips "has reached its end" and that it will begin "gradually decoupling from the game industry," as reported by Taiwanese news site BigGo Finance . That could be an issue for Nintendo, which analyst David Gibson notes uses Macronix as its "main memory chip maker" for physical game cartridges. That ROM production—which has shrunk 39 percent in the last year and now represents just 5 percent of Macronix's business—is being crowded out by production of more lucrative, in-demand chips like NOR- and NAND-based memory and eMMCs, the company said. With Macronix's production capacity stuck at 25,000 12-inch wafers a month—and $1.2 billion in planned new capacity taking a year or more to spin up—less profitable ROM chips are taking up wafer space that can earn more through other types of chips.
